parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-avъšь, past active participle ending of a-conj. verbs.

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ajemъ, present passive participle ending of a- (including some ja-), a/C-, or a/j-conjugation verbs. In Modern Bulgarian, the derivatives constructed with this suffix are interpreted as normal adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming feminine instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: Diminutive form of Bulgarian -ало (-alo) + -ка (-ka), built upon the instrumental suffix Proto-Slavic *-dlo. parole.significato: Deverbal, forming neuter instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-dlo, appended to a-, ja- or a/j-conjugation verbs.

parole.significato: appended to verbs and nouns to form masculine agent nouns denoting profession/occupation; -er, -or
Suffix used to form adjectives from nouns, meaning "having X".
Deverbal from transitive verbs in va-conjugation, forms adjectives expressing capacity, susceptibility, eventuality, or…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-vajemъ, present passive participle ending of va-conjugation verbs. In Modern Bulgarian, the derivatives constructed with this suffix are interpreted as normal adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal from athematic verbs expressing a resultant or a quality induced by a past activity
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-vъšь, past active participle ending. The element -ш (-š) is also found in the old comparative forms of adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal from ě-conj. verbs expressing a resultant or a quality induced by a past activity
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ěvъšь with e-kavian pronunciation of earlier -ě-, past active participle ending of ě- and ě/i-conj. verbs.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming feminine instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: Diminutive form of Bulgarian -ело (-elo) + -ка (-ka), built upon the instrumental suffix Proto-Slavic *-dlo. Occasionally, the suffix can be applied on loanwords ending on -ел-, e.g.: Latin cappella → Bulgarian капела (kapela, “type of hat, cape”) → Bulgarian капелка (kapelka, “small hat, cape”).

parole.significato: Denominal, forming feminine instrumental or resultant nouns with prolonged aspect.
parole.testo: Diminutive form of Bulgarian -ел (-el)/-еля (-elja) + -ка (-ka), built upon the agentative/actionis suffix Proto-Slavic *-ělь.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming neuter instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: Sparsely attested, from an earlier -ѣло (-jělo). Possibly built upon the instrumental suffix Proto-Slavic *-dlo, appended to forms ending in ě-stem (similar to Bulgarian -ало (-alo), -ило (-ilo)), or less likely from Proto-Slavic *-ělь + *-o (“neuter marker”). Virtually unproductive in Modern Bulgar

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming neuter instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-elo, possibly reanalyzed from Etymology 1.

parole.significato: Forms relational adjectives from certain titular nouns.
Deverbal from i-conj. verbs expressing a resultant or a quality induced by a past activity
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ivъšь, past active participle ending of i-conj. verbs.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming feminine instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: Diminutive form of Bulgarian -ило (-ilo) + -ка (-ka), built upon the instrumental suffix Proto-Slavic *-dlo. parole.significato: Deverbal, forming neuter instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-dlo, appended to i-conjugation verbs.

parole.significato: Deverbal from transitive verbs in i-conjugation, forms adjectives expressing capacity, susceptibility, eventuality, or…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *imъ, present passive participle ending of (former) i-conjugation verbs. In Modern Bulgarian, the derivatives constructed with this suffix are interpreted as normal adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forms nouns that express the action of the verb.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-tьba. Originally, the suffix was only applied to verbs with historical infinitives in *-iti, but in modern Bulgarian there are exceptions to that (e.g. върши́тба (văršítba)). Cognates include Serbo-Croatian -идба.

parole.significato: Forms nomina agentis from verbs or adjectives.
Forms masculine patronymic proper names from adjectival forms of personal names; originally denoting membership to a ho…
Creates onomatopoeic verbs from the corresponding interjections.
Forms adjectives from nouns, verbal participles/nouns or adjectives with resultant or approximating meaning: -ish, -abl…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ьlivъ (occasionally Proto-Slavic *-ъlivъ), a combination of the resultative suffix -л (-l) + -ив (-iv).

parole.significato: Forms deverbal nouns denoting a tool or instrument
Forms diminutive agent nouns, often with pejorative meaning
parole.testo: Agentive suffix, back-formed from the adjectival suffix Proto-Slavic *-livъ (“-ly, -ish”) + -ьо (-jo, “diminutive suffix”). Eventually, its application has been extended to form diminutive counter-parts of masculine nouns in -ъл (-ăl), -ел (-el), -ал (-al) (from Proto-Slavic *-ъlъ, *-ьlъ, *-alъ).

parole.significato: Forms male given names from verbs/verbal nouns (usually in i-, ě-conjugation) with approximate meaning great at the ref…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *měrъ (“great”), a frequent element in male given names of Slavic origin.

parole.significato: verbal noun suffix: appended to stems of verbs to form the verbal noun, akin to the gerund in English
Forms adjectives from nouns or adjectives with approximating meaning: -y, -some
Forms adjectives from nouns with approximating meaning: -y, -some
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ovitъ. Specifically, by surface analysis, rebracketing of -ов (-ov) + -ит (-it).

parole.significato: Deverbal from athematic verbs, forms adjectives expressing capacity or proclevity.
parole.testo: Reflects the principal Proto-Slavic present passive ending *-omъ. Mostly unproductive in the colloquial speech, but reintroduced in the Standard language under the influence of Russian loanwords and the efforts of various "purist" movements (during the 18-20th century) for restoring grammatical feat

parole.significato: Derives abstract or collective nouns with expressive connotation: -ity, -ness
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-orьja, cognate with Macedonian -орија (-orija). Equivalent to -ор (-or) + -ия (-ija).

parole.significato: Derives abstract or collective nouns with expressive connotation: -ity, -ness
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-otьja, cognate with Macedonian -отија (-otija). Equivalent to -ота (-ota) + -ия (-ija).

From the Proto-Slavic *-slavъ ending in names such as *Voldislavъ, from Proto-Slavic *slava (“glory, fame”). Via PIE cognate with Ancient Greek κλέος (kléos), κλειτός (kleitós), κλυτός (klutós), note many personal names derived from the terms. Compare typologically Ancient Greek personal names deriv

parole.significato: Deverbal from transitive verbs in ova-conjugation, forms adjectives expressing capacity, susceptibility, eventuality, o…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ujemъ, present passive participle ending of ova-conjugation verbs. In Modern Bulgarian, the derivatives constructed with this suffix are interpreted as normal adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal, forming feminine instrumental or effect nouns.
parole.testo: Built upon the instrumental suffix Proto-Slavic *-dlo on verbs with u- or ova-conjugation, with addition of the diminutive suffix -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: Forms adjectives from nouns, verbal participles/nouns or adjectives with resultant or approximating meaning: -ish, -able
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ъčivъ, *-ьčivъ, a combination of -ък (-ăk) + -ив (-iv). Cognate with Russian -чи́вый (-čívyj).

parole.significato: Forms secondary adjectives with comparative meaning
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Slavic *-ьšь (comparative suffix). Used to form the comparative degree of adjectives, nowadays formed with the prefix по́- (pó-).

parole.significato: Deadjectival, denoting a carrier of the specified property (rare)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ъkъ via Old Church Slavonic -ъкъ (-ŭkŭ).

parole.significato: Forms pet versions of personal names
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ę, applied in diminutive sense on personal names or proper nouns referring to people (nicknames, kit terms, pejorative terms, etc.). Attested more in the Eastern dialects. Cognate with Russian -я (-ja) with similar function.

parole.significato: Deverbal from transitive verbs in ě-conjugation (effectively via a secondary inchoative ěva-derivative), forms adjectiv…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ějemъ, present passive participle ending of ě/i- and ě-conjugation verbs. In Modern Bulgarian, the derivatives constructed with this suffix are interpreted as normal adjectives.

parole.significato: Deverbal from transitive verbs in ja-conjugation, forms adjectives expressing capacity, susceptibility, eventuality, or…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-jajemъ, present passive participle ending of ja-conjugation verbs.

parole.significato: used to describe how two facts are different: whereas, while
elderwort, danewort (shrub of species Sambucus ebulus)
parole.testo: Disputed: * Traditionally has been compared to Ancient Greek ἀκτέᾱ (aktéā, “elder”) (per Miklošič), however, the phonetics do not match; * Per Berneker: possibly of Proto-Slavic origin, related to *xobotъ (“proboscis”), equivalent to *xab- + -ъд (-ăd). Cognate (via other suffixes) to dialectal Serbo

parole.significato: oriole (bird of genus Oriolus), particularly golden oriole (Oriolus oriolus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьvьlga. Old Church Slavonic влъга (vlŭga).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *agnьcь. Akin to а́гне (ágne).

parole.significato: fawn (young roe deer, a mammal of order Artiodactyla)
to exclaim, to cry “ah!”, to sigh (to repeatedly utter “ах” from amazement, delight, pain, pity, suffering, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *axati. By surface analysis, ах (ah) + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: to cry “ах!”, to exclaim, to sigh “ah!” (to repeatedly utter “ах” because of delight, surprise, pain, pity, suffering,…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *axъkati. By surface analysis, ах (ah) + -кам (-kam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bavьnъ. By surface analysis, ба́вя (bávja) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to put off, to postpone, to delay (an action, a response, etc.)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bagrъ (“treated with heat, thermic”). Originally an adjective, which later has been substantivized. The particular hue degree crimson may have been influenced by Oghur *băɣŭr < Proto-Turkic *bakïr (“copper, dirt”) (cf. Chuvash пӑхӑр (păh̬ăr, “copper”)), possibly of Iranian origin.

From (South) Proto-Slavic *gъbanica, *gybanica (“bending, folding”), in reference to the manner of preparation of banitsa (through folding of pastry sheets). Cognate with Macedonian баница (banica), Serbo-Croatian гибаница.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *baňa, itself borrowed from Vulgar Latin baneum. Dialectal meanings may descend from unrelated *bagňa (“moor, bog; brackish water”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *barati (“to seek, to examine”).

parole.significato: fable (a fictitious narrative intended to enforce some useful truth or precept, usually with animals, etc)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *baxurъ /*baxorъ (“intestine”), of uncertain origin. * Possibly an early Turkic borrowing akin to modern Turkish bağır (“bosom”). * If native, probably from Proto-Slavic *baxati (“to fuss, to bluster”) + -ур (-ur).

parole.significato: to exert, to toil, to stupefy
parole.testo: Expressive variant of less common ба́кам with palatalization of -к-, from Proto-Slavic *bakati. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian ба́цити (“to cast, to throw”), Macedonian бакнува (baknuva, “to kiss”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *batę, from *batь + *-ę. Compare to Russian ба́тя (bátja).

parole.significato: to charm, to enchant, to mutter incantations

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bajačь. By surface analysis, ба́я (bája) + -ач (-ač).

parole.significato: to stay keen, to pay attention
used for emphasis in enumeration of entries
parole.testo: Combines: * An emphatic particle derived from Proto-Slavic *ba, *bo, coordinate to де (de), же (že), ле (le). * A form of address borrowed from Ottoman Turkish به, from Byzantine Greek βρέ (bré), probably a colloquial form of Ancient Greek μωρέ (mōré), the vocative of μωρός (mōrós, “dull”).

parole.significato: cursory, fugitive, rough, vague, sketchy, superficial
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *běglъ, an archaic past passive participle of Proto-Slavic *běťi.

parole.significato: herb of genus Pimpinella (particularly Pimpinella saxifraga)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *běditi (“to coerce”). Possibly identical to Etymology 1. See Proto-Slavic entry for further discussion.

parole.significato: to coax, to slander, to convict erroneously
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *běděvati, an iterative form of бедя́ (bedjá, “to coax, to slander”) (among other meanings) + -явам (-javam).

parole.significato: used to threaten or coerce someone to flee away
parole.testo: Contracted from an earlier *бежи (*beži), the imperative of obsolete Proto-Slavic *běžati (“to run”).
From Proto-Slavic *bezdъna, morphologically equivalent to без- (bez-, “without”) + дъ́но (dắno, “bottom”) + -а (-a).

parole.significato: soulless, lifeless, inanimate (without soul, life, spirit, or inner animation)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bezdušьnъ. By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + ду́ша (dúša) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: drought, dry spell (absence of rain, usually for a prolonged period of time)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bezdъždžьje. By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + дъжд (dăžd) + -ие (-ie).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bezzǫbъ. By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + зъб (zăb)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bezimenьnъ. By surface analysis, без (bez) + и́ме (íme) + -ен (-en).
From Proto-Slavic *bezopasьnъ. Analyzable as без- (bez-) + опа́сен (opásen).

parole.significato: insolent, audacious, bold-faced, impertinent (openly disrespectful, rude, or offensively bold)
fearless, intrepid, undaunted, bold, devoid of fear
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bezstrašьnъ. By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + страх (strah) + -ен (-en).

Continues Proto-Slavic *bělěgъ, ultimately of Oghur origin, from Proto-Turkic *bel- (“to denote”). Apparently, the Bulgarian term was reanalyzed to fit the Slavic morphology as if from Proto-Slavic *bělъ (“white”) + -ег (-eg). Cognate with Hungarian bélyeg (“post mark”), Chuvash палӑк (palăk, “sign,

parole.significato: to be white (to appear white or be seen as white)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělěti. By surface analysis, бял (bjal) + -е́я (-éja).

parole.significato: mineral white paint, e.g. zinc white, lead white and titanium white
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělidlo. By surface analysis, бе́ля (bélja, “to make white”) + -ло (-lo)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělina. By surface analysis, бял (bjal, “white”) + -ина́ (-iná, abstract noun formative).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělъka. Doublet of бя́лка (bjálka).

parole.significato: white-haired, grey-haired (having white or grey hair, usually from age)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělovolsъ. By surface analysis, бял (bjal) + -о- (-o-) + влас (vlas)
Re-analyzed from an earlier Proto-Slavic *bělъkъ to rhyme with Bulgarian жълтъ́к (žăltắk, “yolk”). Morphologically equivalent to бял (bjal, “white”) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to converse, to talk, to chat
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *besědovati. By surface analysis, бесе́да (beséda) + -вам (-vam).

parole.significato: would (used with a past active participle to form the conditional mood)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bigrъ/*bigorъ, of unclear origin. Limited to South Slavic languages.

parole.significato: bull (domesticated male bovine used for breeding)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bidlo, morphologically formed from би́я (bíja, “to fight, to beat”) + -ло (-lo, “instrumental suffix”).

parole.significato: way of life, lifestyle (manner of living that reflects the person's values and attitudes)
to excoriate, to castigate, to lambaste, to scourge
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bičevati. By surface analysis, бич (bič) + -увам (-uvam).
Reanalyzed from an earlier благиня́ (blaginjá), from Proto-Slavic *bolgyni. By surface analysis, благ (blag, “gentle”) + -ина (-ina).
From Proto-Slavic *bolgo, a nominalization of благ (blag, “gentle, kind”) + -о (-o).

parole.significato: piece of sod, turf, sward (lump of soil with growing vegetation on it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bolna, formally from Proto-Indo-European *bʰоlH- (“pale, bright”) + -на (-na). Loaned into Aromanian blană (“clump, clod”).

parole.significato: paleness, pallor, pallidness (the quality or state of being pale in colour, especially of the face or skin)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blědostь. By surface analysis, блед (bled) + -ост (-ost)

parole.significato: to flash, to gleam, to shine
to shine, to radiate, to reflect (bright light)
to goggle, to protrude eyes (in order to get a glimpse of sth) + очи́ (očí, “eyes”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *blěščiti (“to glance, to flash”), a denominal inchoative of бля́сък (bljásăk, “glow, glamour”) + -я (-ja). Diachronically related to Etymology 2.
From Proto-Slavic *blizьnakъ. Doublet of близне́ц (bliznéc) and близне́ (blizné) (dated, dialectal). Morphologically equivalent to бли́зо (blízo) + -нак (-nak).
From Proto-Slavic *blizьnьcь via Old Church Slavonic близньць (bliznĭcĭ). Doublet of standard близна́к (bliznák). Morphologically equivalent to бли́зо (blízo, “near”) + -нец (-nec).

parole.significato: near, neighbouring, next door, at short/close range (of a place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *blizъkъ. Formed from an earlier близъ (bliz) + -ък (-ăk) (compare Bulgarian близо (blizo, “nearby”)).

parole.significato: prodigal, lost, straying (having strayed from the right path, especially morally or spiritually)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blǫdьnъ. By surface analysis, блуд (blud) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: fornication, unchastity (sexual relations or conduct regarded as immoral, especially outside marriage)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blǫdьstvo. By surface analysis, блуд (blud) + -ство (-stvo).

parole.significato: to roam, to wander, to rove
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blǫďati, with vocalism levelled to Russian borrowing блуд (blud, “depravity”) (poetic).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blьskъ (“flash”), whence Old Church Slavonic бльскъ (blĭskŭ). The semantic development seems to have been “flash, flicker” → “sudden movement” → “strike”.

parole.significato: to surge, to gush, to flood (of liquid)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bľuti (“to surge”), merged with an onomatopoeic element (cf. dial. бю́вам (bjúvam, “to puke”)).
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *blędь: * For obsolete sense: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic блѧдь (blędĭ); * For derogatory sense: Borrowed from Russian блядь (bljadʹ).

parole.significato: broad bean (an edible bean that has broad seeds (Vicia faba))

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bogatъ. By surface analysis, бог (bog, “god”) + -ат (-at).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bogatьstvo. By surface analysis, бога́т (bogát) + -ство (-stvo).

parole.significato: sting (with a needle or a sharp object)
to prick, to sting, to stab (to pierce or wound with a sharp point)

parole.testo: The singular form is from Proto-Slavic *bodylъ, while the plural technically reflects Proto-Slavic *bodъľь (expected is *бодили).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *božьjь. By surface analysis, бог (bog) + -и (-i).

parole.significato: beating, thrashing, drubbing, whopping, whipping, flogging, leathering, knock-about, punch-up, caning
parole.testo: O-grade deverbal of би́я (bíja, “to beat”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *bojь.
From Proto-Slavic *boľь (“pain”). Originally a feminine i-stem.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bolěstь. By surface analysis, бол (bol, “pain, ache”) + -ест (-est).

parole.significato: to care, to be concerned, to worry (about someone or something)
pain, ache (unpleasant physical, sensory experience physically felt in some part of the body usually caused by injury o…
parole.testo: Diminutive of Proto-Slavic *boľь. Equivalent to бол (bol) + -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: pine, pine tree (tall, evergreen coniferous tree with cones)
to handle, to deal with, to work with
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *boraviti, of disputed origin. Limited to South Slavic. * Per BER, possibly akin to бо́ря (bórja, “to wrestle”) + -авя (-avja). * Per Miklošič, from a hypothetical *bvor-, cognate with the copula *byti (“to be”).

parole.significato: fight, battle (a physical confrontation or combat between two or more people or groups)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *borьba. Morphologically equivalent to бо́ря (bórja, “to fight, to wrestle”) + -ба (-ba).
From Proto-Slavic *borьcь, morphologically from бо́ря (bórja, “to wrestle”) + -ец (-ec).

parole.significato: to wrestle, to fight, to combat
barefoot, bare-footed (having no shoes or socks on the feet)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bosonogъ. By surface analysis, бос (bos) + -о- (-o-) + нога (noga)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *boturь (“plant stem, sprout”), syntactically parseable as боте́я (botéja, “to grow, to flourish”) (dialectal) + -ур (-ur). Related via another vowel grade to dialectal Russian бата́рь (batárʹ, “weed”) and via another suffix to Russian боту́н (botún, “altai onion”). For t
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bojьkъ. By surface analysis, бой (boj, “fight”) + -ък (-ăk).
From Proto-Slavic *bordà, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *bardā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰardʰéh₂.

parole.significato: to furrow, to plow, to make furrows

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *borniteľь; equivalent to браня (branja, “to defend, to resist”) + -тел (-tel).

parole.significato: to shield, to protect, to defend
flour, floury (relating to flour; made from or containing flour)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *boršьnьnъ. By surface analysis, бра́шно (brášno) + -ен (-en)

Formally reflecting an earlier *bergališče, from the same origin as Брега́лница (Bregálnica, “Bregalnica”) (hydronym). Either derived from Proto-Slavic *bergъ (“coast, bank”) or possibly of Paleo-Balkan origin akin to Thracian Βέργα (Bérga), Dacian Bregedáva. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰe

parole.significato: to traverse, to stroll, to wade
to grunt, to wheeze (to puff heavily)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bręcati, of onomatopoeic origin.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bridъkъ (“sharp”). By surface analysis, бридя́ (bridjá, “to bite (for wind)”) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: pocketknife, folding knife, penknife (a pocket knife that closes into a slotted handle)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *britva. By surface analysis, бри́я (bríja) + -тва (-tva).

parole.significato: to shave, to trim (beard or fur)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *briti, nowadays obsolete. Superseded by synonymous Bulgarian бръ́сна (brắsna).

parole.significato: ford (location where a stream is shallow and the bottom has good footing, making it possible to cross from one side to…

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *broščь, of unclear origin. Has been compared with Latin bractea (“foil”).
Deverbal of Proto-Slavic *brukati /*břukati (“to pop off, to burst”).

parole.significato: to shake off, to thrash (fruits from a tree)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bьrgъlъ, *bьrgъlězъ (“nuthatch”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian бр̀глијез, Slovene bȓglez, Polish bargiel. Further akin to Russian берглéз (bergléz, “goldfinch”).

parole.significato: to taste tarry, poignant (for spoilt food)
parole.testo: Probably an essive derivative of Proto-Slavic *brьzgati (“to brisk, to poign; to stale (for food)”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to sprinkle, to drizzle, to strew
parole.testo: Probably onomatopoeic, perhaps with original meaning “to popple” (cf. synonymous шуртя́ (šurtjá)). BER enlists as cognates Serbo-Croatian бри̏згати, Russian бры́згать (brýzgatʹ), etc.; thus, presumably from an earlier Proto-Slavic *brъzgati (“to strew, to splatter”). Could also reflect *brьzgati (“t
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *brъzda, whence Old Church Slavonic бръзда (brŭzda, “halter”), Czech brzda (“brake”).

parole.significato: beetle, bug (holometabolous insect of order Coleoptera)
parole.testo: Of onomatopoeic nature, from Proto-Slavic *brǫbarъ. By surface analysis, *бръмб- (*brămb-, “buzzing”) + -ар (-ar).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *brъskati, an inchoative sk-extension of *brъsati (“to sweep”).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *brъsnǫti (“to sweep”), secondarily influenced by obsolete бри́я (bríja, “to shave”). The two meanings are still treated as distinct lemmas in Gerov's dictionary: respectively under бръ́снѫ (brắsnǫ, “to sweep”) and брь́снѫ (brʹ́snǫ, “to shave”).

parole.significato: stock of leafage and young twigs used as fodder for farm animals
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *brъstь (= *brъd- (“brittle, frail”) + *-tь). Akin to English brittle.

parole.significato: to blather, to prattle, to chatter
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bъrtviti, a causative iterative of obsolete *bъrtva (“prattle”) (= *bъr- (onomatopoeic root) + *-tva).

parole.significato: to jabber, to twaddle, to prattle
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Slavic *brъšč- (“clatter”) + -олевя (-olevja). Akin to dial. Bulgarian бръ́скам (brắskam, “to prod, to clack”), Slovene bŕskati (“to browse, to tackle”).
From Proto-Slavic *buba, *bǫba. Akin to Albanian bubë (“silkworm pupa”), Latvian bubulis (“knot, node”).
From Proto-Slavic *budьnъ; equivalent to будя (budja, “to awake”) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to wake (up), to awaken (to make somebody stop sleeping)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *buditi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *báudīˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰowdʰéyeti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *buza. Likely a substratum word, related to Albanian buzë and Romanian buză (“lip”).

parole.significato: beech, beech tree (tree of genus Fagus)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bukъ, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *bōkō.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *buna. By surface analysis, буя́ (bujá, “to rage up, to rebel”) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: to incite, to stir up, to agitate (to provoke someone to rebellion, unrest, or resistance)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *burьjanъ. Equivalent to dialectal буря́ се (burjá se, “to surge, to rave”) + -ян (-jan).

parole.significato: to push, to thrust, to shove
to batter, to bang, to clap [smth.] with accompanying dull noise

parole.testo: Technically reflecting Proto-Slavic *buxyrъ, probably with original meaning bulged, bloated creature. If correct, then derived from бу́хвам (búhvam, “to bulge, to bloat, to tumefy”) + -ер (-er). Alternatively, modified from dialectal Bulgarian бу́га (búga, “bull”) (of Turkic origin) + -ер (-er) due

parole.significato: to push, to poke, to prod (with a tool)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bud- / *but- + -цам (-cam, expressive verbal suffix) (cf. бо́цам (bócam) < бода́ (bodá, “to pierce”), кле́цам (klécam) < кля́кам (kljákam, “to squat”)). Akin to English beat.

parole.significato: to pin, to pierce, to impale
parole.testo: Of expressive origin, from an earlier Proto-Slavic *bučiti (i-conjugation).

parole.significato: to clang, to rumble, to echo (of natural noise)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bučati (ě/i-conjugation), of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: to flourish, to grow rampant (of plant, weed)

parole.testo: Diminutive of an earlier Proto-Slavic *bъdьňa + -е (-e, diminutive suffix). Possibly of substrate origin, akin to Latin butina (“bottle”), Ancient Greek πῡτῑ́νη (pūtī́nē, “flask”), possibly Proto-Germanic *puttaz (“pot”).

parole.significato: to vomit, to puke; to belch, to burp
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bľьvati, iterative or punctual counterpart to dialectal блю́я (bljúja, “to gush, to surge”), бю́вам (bjúvam, “to vomit”).

parole.significato: to rave, to sleepwalk → to walk, roam aimlessly
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *blǫdati with metathesis of earlier *-лъ- > -ъл-; equivalent to блу́да (blúda, “delusion, corruption”) (dialectal) + -ам (-am).
From Proto-Slavic *blъxa (“flea”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *blúšāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *plus- (“flea”).
Derived from Proto-Slavic *bry (v-stem) (the modern term has been reanalyzed as an a-stem).

parole.significato: fast, swift, quick, rapid, sweeping, fleet
to hurry, to hasten, to rush
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bъrzati. Morphologically equivalent to бърз (bărz, “fast”) + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: stretch of a river with swift current, a rapid
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bъrzьjь; equivalent to бърз (bărz, “fast, swift”) + -ей (-ej).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bъrkъ sg (“whisker”), *bъrky du. Further origin is disputed. Possibly related to бъ́ркам (bắrkam, “to poke”) (see literature for further discussion).

parole.significato: to stir, to mingle, to blend up
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *brъkati (“to shove, to thrush”).
From Proto-Slavic *bъrna. Akin to Armenian բերան (beran, “mouth”).

parole.significato: to wrinkle, to furrow, to make wrinkled (to draw the skin, especially the forehead, face, brows, or nose, into wrinkles)
to sweep, to wipe, to swab (with a mop)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bъči (jū-stem). Either Germanic borrowing or derived from the root of бъ́кел (bắkel), бъ́клица (bắklica, “keg”) + -ва (-va) (itself of uncertain origin).
From бял (bjal, “white”) + дроб (drob, “liver”). This second component ultimately stems from Proto-Slavic *drobъ (literally “organ”).

parole.significato: Forms verbs with the meaning of
to allure, to entice [an animal] with a call

parole.testo: Blend of: * Inherited from Proto-Slavic *valъ (“surge, wave”). * Resultant noun of валя́ (valjá, “to tumble, to plummet”), iterative verb from *valъ. * Instrumental noun of ва́лям (váljam, “to roll”), causative/inchoative verb from *valъ. * Technical meaning borrowed from Russian вал (val), ultimate
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *valežь. By surface analysis, валя (valja, “to fall, to crumble, to revolve”) + -еж (-ež).

parole.significato: to fall (of rain, snow or hail)
full form of the second-person plural pronoun in the dative case, used as the indirect object of a verb; to you, for yo…
to hurry, to make haste, to rush

your, yours (polite form of the second-person singular or plural possessive determiner/pronoun)
to sculpt, to model, to mould
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vajati, of disputed further origin.

Оf disputed origin: * Per Vl. Georgiev (BER): From a dialectal variant of ве́жда (véžda, “eyebrow”) + -ав (-av) (compare Macedonian веѓа (veǵa)) that has spread to other dialects. Effectively reflecting Proto-Slavic *věďavъ, probably originally meaning staring, glaring, focused. Compare colloquial B
From Proto-Slavic *vesti. In Modern Bulgarian, its function has been mostly supplanted by the causative водя (vodja).

parole.significato: malevolent female mythical creature, witch, ghost
parole.testo: Deverbal of Proto-Slavic *věděti (“to know, to wit”). Equivalent to Old Church Slavonic вѣдь (vědĭ, “knowledge”) + + -а (-a). Compare ве́щица (véštica), Russian ве́дьма (védʹma).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vědomъ, present passive (perfective) participle of *věděti (“to know”). Equivalent to dialectal вям (vjam, “to be familiar”) + -ом (-om).

parole.significato: clear, bright, cloudless (of weather, sky, morning, day, etc.: without clouds, mist, or gloom; full of light)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vedrъ, akin to English weather.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vęzati (a/j-conjugation). Synchronically, a semelfactive of Bulgarian ве́за (véza, “to embroidier”).

parole.significato: to embroider, to adorn, to stitch

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vęzьba. Morphologically equivalent to везя́ (vezjá, “to thread, to embroider”) + -ба (-ba).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vęzьmo. By surface analysis, вез (vez, “embroidery”) + -мо (-mo).

parole.significato: to claim, to state, to tell

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *věnьcь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *waiˀníkas, from Proto-Indo-European *woyh₁níkos.

parole.significato: bride-price, bride-gift (price paid on behalf of the groom to bride's parents)
chain, towline (a series of interconnected rings or links)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *veriga, derived from the root of вра (vra, “to insert”) + -ига (-iga).

parole.significato: windy, wind-swept (characterized by wind; exposed to or full of wind)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *větrьnъ. By surface analysis, вя́тър (vjátăr) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: to fade away, to wilt (of plants)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vędnǫti. According to Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary, the epenthetic -х- is due to folk association with synonymous съ́хна (sắhna, “to get dry, to wither”).

parole.significato: worn out, wilted, faded, shabby, dilapidated
parole.testo: Metathesized from Proto-Slavic *vetъxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wétušas, from Proto-Indo-European *wet-.

parole.significato: eternal, everlasting, endless (having no beginning or end, or lasting forever)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *večerъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wékeras, from Proto-Indo-European *wekʷsperos.
Confluence of Proto-Slavic *věťь (“indicative”) (from *věťati (“to claim”)) and *věščь (“proficient”) (from *věděti (“to foresee, to know”)). Nowadays, attested mainly in derivatives.

parole.significato: to prophesy, to foretell, to presage
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *věščati. By surface analysis, вещ (vešt, “proficient”) + -ая (-aja).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *věja, related via o-ablaut to Bulgarian ви́я (víja, “to turn, to twine”).

parole.significato: mutual, reciprocal (felt, done, or existing equally between two or more persons, sides, or things)
to take (to grasp with the hands)

parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Slavic *vidati (“to observe”), with the semantic shift to see → to watch over → to take care of → to cure. Cognate with Macedonian вида (vida, “to heal”), Serbo-Croatian vídati (“to cure”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vydra, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ūdrāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *udréh₂, the feminine form of *udrós.

parole.significato: to scream, to shout, to yell
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vykáti. By surface analysis, ви́я (víja, “howl”) + -кам (-kam).

parole.significato: to shout, to cry out, to call out (to utter something loudly, suddenly, or with force)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vidla, an instrumental noun from ви́я (víja, “to twine, to curve”) + -ла (-la, “instrumental suffix”).

parole.significato: vila (mythological creature from Slavic mythology similar to nymphs and fairies)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vila, probably akin to Bulgarian ви́хър (víhăr, “gale, wind torrent”), вие́лица (viélica, “blizzard”). Another hypothesis (per Vasmer) relates the word to Proto-Indo-European *weh₁y- (“to chase, to pursue”), presumably with an original meaning prosecutor, haunter.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vidlica. By surface analysis, ви́ла (víla, “pitchfork”) + -ица (-ica)

parole.significato: to blame, to accuse, to condemn
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *viniti. Synchronically, a causative-iterative of вина́ (viná, “guilt”).

parole.significato: to protrude, to erect, to prick
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *viriti, combining: * An expressive variant of Bulgarian вра (vra, “to thrust into, to insert”); * Iterative-causative of Bulgarian вря (vrja, “to boil”).

parole.significato: to hang, to dangle (to hang down or remain suspended from something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *visnǫti. By surface analysis, вися́ (visjá) + -на (-na)
From Proto-Slavic *vitьlь, cognate with Old Church Slavonic витьль (vitĭlĭ), Macedonian вител (vitel).
From Proto-Slavic *vitъkъ. Morphologically equivalent ви́я (víja, “to wind, to twine”) + -тък (-tăk).

parole.significato: whirlwind, vortex, eddy (a rapidly rotating movement of air, dust, water, smoke, etc.)
to bend, to twist, to curve
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *viti. Some of the derived terms, such as надви́я (nadvíja, “to overwhelm”), are technically derived from a homonymous **viti (“to chase”), which has attested cognates in Baltic, but has been lost in Slavic. See вина́ (viná, “guilt”) for another derivative from the same r

parole.significato: to howl, to wail (of a person, animal, wind, or sound: to make a long, plaintive or high-pitched sound)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vъkusьnъ. By surface analysis, вкус (vkus) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: moisture (very small drops of water that are present in the air, on a surface or in a substance)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *volka. Synchronically, deverbal from вла́ча (vláča, “to tug, to pull”).

parole.significato: fibre, filament, thread, fiber (a single elongated piece of a given material, roughly round in cross-section, often twi…
hair (a single hair of a human or animal)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *volxъ, itself of Germanic origin.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *velčugo. By surface analysis, влека́ (vleká, “to drag, to pull”) + -юго (-jugo).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vodъ, an о-grade action noun of Bulgarian веда́ (vedá, “to haul, to conduct”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *voditi. Synchronically, causative-iterative of вод (vod, “conduct”).

From Proto-Slavic *vojevoda, identical to вой (voj, “army”) (dated) + -е- (-e-) + вод (vod, “conduction”), a calque of Ancient Greek στρατηγός (stratēgós) (or formed in the same logic as it). Compare the Germanic borrowing херцо́г (hercóg, “duke”) from Proto-Germanic *harjatugô (“army commander”).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *voňati. Synchronically, a factitive verb of Bulgarian воня́ (vonjá, “odour”).

parole.significato: to thrust, to drive into, to shove

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vorbьcь, technically a diminutive of врабе́й (vrabéj) (obsolescent, formal) + -ец (-ec).

parole.significato: edema, tumefaction (in result of an injury)
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Slavic *vorga, akin to Proto-Slavic *vergti, *vьrgati (“to roll; to cast”). No exact cognates are attested in other Slavic languages. Probably further akin to Proto-Germanic *warkiz (“ache”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *voržiti. By surface analysis, враг (vrag, “enemy”) + -я (-ja); alternatively derivable from вра́жи (vráži, “fiendish”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *voržati. Morphologically, an essive counter-part to Etymology 1.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vornъ. Attested in various toponyms like Ва́рна (Várna), Вра́ня (Vránja), Вра́ница (Vránica).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vortъ. Synchronically, an instrumental noun of (dialectal) вра́тя (vrátja, “to turn”).

parole.significato: tansy (flower of genus Tanacetum, most often of species Tanacetum vulgare)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vortika. Parsable as вратя (vratja, “to turn”) + -ика (-ika).

parole.significato: harm, damage, detriment (something that harms, damages, or injures someone’s interests, rights, health, reputation, or…
parole.testo: Related to Old Church Slavonic врѣдъ m (vrědŭ, “wound, illness”), dialectal Bulgarian вред (vred) from Proto-Slavic *verdъ (“injury”), but not certainly how. From Proto-Slavic *vъrędьnъ (“fit, organized”); equivalent to вред (vred, “in order, around”) + -ен (-en). Cognate with Macedonian вреден (vreden, “hardworking, handy”).

From Proto-Slavic *verdьnъ (“worthy”). Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary does not distinguish between this form and Etymology 2, but thorough analysis demonstrates that the etymons are distinct. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian врије́дан (“worthy”), Macedonian вреден (vreden, “valuable”).

parole.significato: to harm, to damage, to do mischief (to someone or something)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *veržь m, *verže n. Cognate with Lithuanian veržỹs (“rope”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vermenьnъ. By surface analysis, вре́мен- (vrémen-, “time”) + -ен (-en).
Formally from Proto-Slavic *verťь (yo-stem), a variant of *verťa f.

parole.significato: to squeal, to bleat, to whine
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *verščati (cf. Russian вереща́ть (vereščátʹ)) or *vьręščati (Gerov), of expressive origin. By surface analysis, вря́сък (vrjásăk, “squeal”) + -я (-ja).
From Proto-Slavic *vьrvь, deverbal of *verti. Cognate with Slovene vrv, Serbo-Croatian врвца/vrvca and врпца/vrpca, Russian верёвка (verjóvka).
From Proto-Slavic *vьrstь (i-stem), a deverbal action noun of въ́ртя (vắrtja, “to turn, to rotate”).

From Proto-Slavic *vьrtъ (“turn, enclosure”), cognate with Serbo-Croatian вр̏т and akin to верт in Russian вертоград (vertograd). Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьrěva, of onomatopoeic origin. Loaned into Romanian and Aromanian vreavă, avrevi (“babble”).
Neuter of Proto-Slavic *vьśь (“all”), from an earlier *vьxо (prior to Slavic third palatalization).

parole.significato: maternal uncle, the brother of someone's mother
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *ujь plus a suffix, cognate with Serbo-Croatian ујак/ujak, also ујко/ujko, Slovene ujac, Russian вуй (vuj) and уй (uj), Ukrainian вуй (vuj) and Slovak ujo.
From Proto-Slavic *ǫbьlъ. In some dialects, suffix -ел (-el) generalized to reflect Proto-Slavic *-elъ, under the influence of synonymous сту́бел (stúbel, “delved well, trough”).
From въ́гъл (vắgăl) + -ен (-en), from Proto-Slavic *ǫglь, originally only an adjective.
From Proto-Slavic *vъz (“above”), continuing Old Church Slavonic въз (vŭz).

parole.significato: binder, fastener (of bag, shoes, cloths, apron)
parole.testo: Per BER, a recent derivative, probably from contamination of ве́зя (vézja, “to web, to braid”) and въже́ (văžé, “rope”). Formally equivalent to Proto-Slavic *ǫzъ (“bond, tie”) (whence Old Church Slavonic съвѫзъ (sŭvǫzŭ, “link, conjoinment”)), *ǫza (“chain”) (whence Old Church Slavonic ѫза (ǫza, “sha

parole.significato: view, opinion, belief (a way of thinking about something; an opinion or conviction)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vъzględъ, from *vъz- + *ględěti. By surface analysis, въз- (văz-) + глед (gled). Cognate with Russian взгля́д (vzgljád).

parole.significato: air (gases making up the atmosphere of a planet)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vъzduxъ. By surface analysis, въз- (văz-) + дух (duh).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vъzkrьsnǫti. Compare with Old Czech vzkřesnúti, Old Church Slavonic въскрьснѫти (vŭskrĭsnǫti), Old East Slavic въскрьснути (vŭskrĭsnuti), Serbo-Croatian у̀скрснути.

parole.significato: to object, to protest (to express disagreement with someone or something; to oppose verbally)
age (duration of being from birth until present)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vъzorstь, a deverbal action noun of възраста́ pf (văzrastá), възра́ствам impf (văzrástvam, “to grow up, to mature”). Masculine declension reflecting Etymology 2.

parole.significato: to delight, to enchant (to cause someone to feel admiration, delight, or strong approval)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьlčьjь. By surface analysis, вълк (vălk) + -и (-i). Cognates include Serbo-Croatian вучји, Russian во́лчий (vólčij) and Polish wilczy.

parole.significato: to raise voice, to yell, to weep

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *vьrdlo, an instrumental noun of вря (vrja, “to spring, to boil”) + -ло (-lo, “instrumental suffix”). Probably originally meaning pole, beam as in Ukrainian верло́ (verló, “pole, bat”), dialectal ви́рло (výrlo) or the derivative Bulgarian върли́на (vărlína, “long rod”) (cognate wit
From Proto-Slavic *vьr(t)nǫti (with regular deletion of *-t- before *-n-). Doublet of връ́тна (vrắtna).

Probably a derivative from an obsolete verb *върпя (*vărpja) + -ина (-ina), from Proto-Slavic *vьrpati, *vьrpiti. Akin to dialectal Slovene vŕpati (“to turn, to grab, to ditch”), dialectal Russian верпе́ть (verpétʹ, “to spring”). Also probably related to Proto-Slavic *vorpъ > dialectal Russian вороп

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьrtъpъ. Attested with the meaning “cave, garden” in Old Church Slavonic врьтъпъ (vrĭtŭpŭ), whence Romanian Vârtop (toponym). By surface analysis, въ́ртя (vắrtja, “to turn, to whirl”) + -оп (-op).

parole.significato: to turn, to rotate, to spin, to screw
to carry out, to perform, to do (an action, task, etc.)
having facial hair (in particular mustache, goatee, or whiskers)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *ǫsatъ, formed as въс (văs, “facial hair”) (dialectal) + -ат (-at). Cognate with Russian уса́тый (usátyj).
Action noun of въста́на (văstána, “to rebel, to raise up”) + -ие (-ie). Formally reflects Proto-Slavic *vъstanьje. Cognate with Russian встава́ние (vstavánije), восста́ние (vosstánije, “uprising”).

parole.significato: limp, flaccid, wilted (lacking firmness, freshness, or vitality)
faithfulness, loyalty, fidelity, devotion (the quality of being faithful, loyal, or devoted to someone or something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *věrьnostь. By surface analysis, ве́рен (véren) + -ост (-ost).

parole.significato: hornbeam (especially, the common hornbeam or European hornbeam (Carpinus betulus))

parole.testo: Onomatopoeic, from Proto-Slavic *gavъ. Compare Latin gāvia (“type of bird”).
From Proto-Slavic *gavědь, originally meaning “disorganized, orderless pack (of people, animals, objects)” → “wild stock”.

parole.significato: to bark, to roar, to caw
parole.testo: Onomatopoeic, from гав (gav, “bark, caw”) + -кам (-kam). Compare Proto-Slavic *gavati.

parole.significato: mockery, ridicule, derision, jeering (mocking, insulting, or humiliating treatment)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gavьra. Compare га́вря се (gávrja se).

parole.significato: to tell fortunes, to divine (to predict the future by cards, coffee grounds, palm reading, or other means)
to feel nauseous, to feel sick
to caress, to pet, to stroke affectionately

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gavornъ, a conflation of the call га-га (ga-ga, “kra-kra”) + вран (vran, “crow”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gasidlo. By surface analysis, гася́ (gasjá) + -ило (-ilo).

parole.significato: to go out, to die out, to be extinguished (of a flame, fire, light, etc.: to gradually stop burning or shining)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gasnǫti. Cognates include Russian га́снуть (gásnutʹ), Serbo-Croatian га̏снути /gȁsnuti and Polish gasnąć.

parole.significato: to extinguish, to put out (to stop a fire, flame, or burning object from burning)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gybati. Etymologically identical with Old Church Slavonic гꙑбати (gybati, “to perish”), whence modern Bulgarian заги́вам (zagívam), поги́вам (pogívam). Modern semantics attested in prefixed прѣгꙑбати (prěgybati, “to bend, to shove”).

Reflects Proto-Slavic *gybъkъ (“flexible”), possibly borrowed from Russian ги́бкий (gíbkij). Cognate with Macedonian гибок (gibok) (dialectal). Morphologically identical to ги́бам (gíbam, “to flex, to hang, to thread”) (dialectal) + -ък (-ăk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gybnǫti. By surface analysis, ги́бам (gíbam) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: to carve, to clear off, to obviate

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *golvьňa: * Per BER: derived from Bulgarian глава́ (glavá, “head”), гла́вен (gláven, “main, capital”) (see Etymology 3). * Per Machek, Stankiewicz: probably from an earlier *golv- (“to decay, to languish”) + -ня (-nja), akin to Lithuanian gélti (“to sting”), pagalỹs (“log
From Proto-Slavic *golmavъ. Morphologically equivalent to гла́ма (gláma, “large rock”) (dialectal) + -ав (-av).

parole.significato: voice, vocal (relating to the voice or produced by the voice)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *golsьnъ. By surface analysis, глас (glas) + -ен (-en)
From Proto-Slavic *golsovati, composed of *golsъ (“voice”) + *-ovati (verbal suffix), equivalent to глас (glas) + -увам (-uvam).

parole.significato: to read, to say (of a message, document, etc.)
to look at (transitive or with към (kăm) + object)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gleznъ with apparent splitting of the cluster -zn-.
From Proto-Slavic *gliba, akin to English cliff.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *glina, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gléiˀnāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *gleh₁y-.

parole.significato: clay, clayey, argillaceous (relating to clay or consisting of clay)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gliněnъ. By surface analysis, гли́на (glína) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: to fine, to mulct, to amerce (to impose a fine)
node, knar, snag, knob (of surface or plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gluďь, distantly related to English clot.

parole.significato: mockery, ridicule, derision (an act or expression of mocking, ridiculing, or making fun of someone or something)
to joke, to tease, to jest (to joke or tease someone, often playfully)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *glupavъ. Morphologically equivalent to глуп (glup, “stupid”) (dialectal) + -ав (-av).
Possibly from archaic глуп (glup, “stupid”) + -ост (-ost, “-ity”, nominalizing suffix) or Proto-Slavic *glupostь.

parole.significato: depth, deepness, profundity (the quality or state of being deep)
to go silent, to diminish in volume (of sound, noise)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gnězdo, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nisdan, from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós.

parole.significato: to oppress, to tyrannize (to rule over a society with violence or terror)
nit (the egg of a louse, especially one attached to hair or clothing)
to rot, to decay, to putrefy

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gnusьnъ. By surface analysis, гнус (gnus) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to be disgusted, to be repulsed (to feel strong physical or moral disgust toward someone or something)
to venerate, to regard with high esteem
speech (faculty of speech; session of speaking)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *govoriti, from Proto-Indo-European *gewH- (“to call, cry”).

parole.significato: young calf presented as a dowery
parole.testo: Standardized form of dialectal годиш (godiš), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *godiťь. By surface analysis, год (god, “year”) + -ищ (-išt).

parole.significato: to betroth, to engage (to arrange a marriage engagement)

parole.testo: Simplification of an earlier гостба (gostba), from Proto-Slavic *gostьba. Morphologically equivalent to гост (gost, “guest”) + -ба (-ba). Originally meant food that is served to guests.
From Proto-Slavic *gojь, an action noun of Bulgarian гоя́ (gojá, “to feed, to provide”).

From the fossilized locative or dative singular of Proto-Slavic *gorà (“mountain”, literally “to/on the mountain”); compare гора́ (gorá, “mountain”, archaic). Stress shift onto the stem is expected in the locative singular but not the dative singular. However, the parallelism with до́лу (dólu, “down
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gořestь. By surface analysis, го́рък (górăk, “bitter, sorrowful”) + -ест (-est).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *goręťь. By surface analysis, горя́ (gorjá) + -ещ (-ešt). Doublet of горя́щ (gorjášt), a modern participle based on Russian and Church Slavonic.
From Proto-Slavic *gorьčivъ, an extended form of *gorьkъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gorьkъ. By surface analysis, горя́ (gorjá, “to burn”) + -ък (-ăk). ́
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gostь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gastís, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis. Doublet of го́стенин (góstenin).

parole.significato: fine, cool, pleasantly (of situation, environment, or mood)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gotoviti. Cognate with Macedonian готви (gotvi), Russian гото́вить (gotóvitʹ), Polish gotować.

parole.significato: to fatten, to fatten up (to feed an animal or person abundantly)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grabežь. By surface analysis, гра́бя (grábja, “to steal, to rob”) + -еж (-ež).

parole.significato: carding tool, comber, hatchel (tool for carding and napping fabrics such as linen and flax)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grabľi du, a fossilized dual of *grabľa (ja-stem). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian гра̏бље f pl, Slovene gráblje f pl (from proper plural *grabľẹ pl instead). By surface analysis, гра́бя (grábja, “to snatch”) + -ля (-lja).

parole.significato: hillfort (the remains or site of an old fortified settlement, fortress, or stronghold)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gordišče. By surface analysis, град (grad) + -и́ще (-íšte)
Result noun of onomatopoeic гра́я (grája, “to conjure a call, to play music”) + -й (-j), from Proto-Slavic *grajь.
Onomatopoeic, from Proto-Slavic *grakъ. Compare Latin grāculus (“jackdaw”) (whence English grackle).

parole.significato: to caw, to croak, to screech
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grakati (“to caw, croak”), ultimately, onomatopoeic, from the call гра-гра (gra-gra) + -кам (-kam).

parole.significato: tree's canopy, crown (collection of tree's branches and foliage)

parole.testo: Dialectal word for orange from Proto-Slavic *granivъ; equivalent to гран (gran, “pus”) (dialectal) + -ив (-iv). Superseded in the standard language by the loanword Bulgarian оранжев (oranžev, “orange”).

parole.significato: border, boundary, frontier (line or demarcation separating regions)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *granica. Synchronically parsable as гран (gran, “edge, verge”) + -ица (-ica).
From Proto-Slavic *gorpavъ, *xorpavъ. Derived from гра́па (grápa, “roughness, unevenness”) (dialectal) + -ав (-av). Akin to Macedonian рапав (rapav), Serbo-Croatian хра̏пав, Polish chropowaty.

parole.significato: pea (a plant, Pisum sativum, member of the legume (Fabaceae) family)
to row, to pull (at the oars), to scull, to paddle
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gretì (“to dig, to scrape, to rake”).

parole.significato: comb, hair-comb, curry-comb, hackle (toothed implement for grooming the hair)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grebenь (n-stem), equivalent to греба́ (grebá, “to comb”) + -ен (-en).
From Proto-Slavic *grebьnъ. Equivalent to гре́ба (gréba, “to rake, to row”) + -ен (-en).
From Proto-Slavic *gręda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *grindā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrendʰ-.

parole.significato: to come, to advance, to progress
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grędati, a secondary variant of *gręsti (whence Old Church Slavonic грѧсти (gręsti), dial. Bulgarian гре́нда (grénda)).
From Proto-Slavic *grezdьjь; equivalent to грезд (grezd, “shoot, nub”) + -ей (-ej).
Substantivized form of Proto-Slavic *gręzьnъ (“muddy, sludgy”) or from *gręzenь. Akin to Ukrainian грузь (hruzʹ, “swamp”), Polish grąz (“bog, mire”). Nowadays mainly attested in toponyms.

parole.significato: to proliferate, to get much fruit (of plants)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grěxnǫti (“to clamour”). Akin to Lithuanian grekšė́ti (“to creak”), gar̃sas (“grunt”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grěxovьnъ. By surface analysis, грях (grjah) + -овен (-oven).

parole.significato: to sin, to commit a sin, to transgress

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *grěti. Cognate with Russian греть (gretʹ, “to heat”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grivьna. By surface analysis, гри́ва (gríva, “mane”) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: to gnaw (at), to nibble (at), to eat into
fruits of plants from genus Vitis
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *grozdьje (“grapes”), originally a collective sg. tantum with meaning cluster of grapes. Morphologically, equivalent to грозд (grozd, “single grape”) + -е (-e).

From Proto-Slavic *grozьnъ. For the meaning development compare English ugly (< Old Norse uggligr < uggr); Russian стра́шный (strášnyj) (< Proto-Slavic *strašьnъ < *straxъ); Latin foedus (< Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyh₂-).

parole.significato: to disfigure, to deform, to uglify
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *groziti, а causative-iterative verb of obsolescent гроза́ (grozá, “menace”). The literary meaning is borrowed from Russian грози́ть (grozítʹ, “to threaten”).

parole.significato: to clap, to strike with a dull object
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *groxati, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: to collapse, to break down, to become exhausted, to become decrepit (from exhaustion)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grǫbъ /*grubъ via a Western dialect; possibly reinforced by Russian гру́бый (grúbyj).

parole.significato: to thresh, to bash grain (in order to separate the seeds from the husks)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *grъmъ. Akin to Slovene gȓm and Serbo-Croatian гр̏м / gȑm. Further cognates include Sanskrit गुल्म (gulma, “shrub”).

parole.significato: to lose (to cause something to cease to be in one's possession or capability)

parole.testo: Formally reflects Proto-Slavic *gǫda (“funnel-like shape”), akin to Serbo-Croatian гу̀дура (“sharp gorge, ravine”) (dialectal). Further origin uncertain.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gǫděti, spread from a western dialect.

From Proto-Slavic *gulьja, cognate with Russian гулья (gulʹja, “swelling”) (dialectal), Ukrainian гуля (hulja, “swelling”) (dialectal), Slovak huľa (“ball”). Formed from the same root as Bulgarian жу́ля (žúlja, “to rub”), with the collective marker -ия (-ija).

parole.significato: feast, spree, revelry, binge, blow-out, jamboree, randan, drinking-bout, drinking-party, carousal
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *guľajь. Morphologically, from гуля́я (guljája, “to feast”) + -яй (-jaj).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gurьlъ, cognate with Macedonian гурелка (gurelka).
From Proto-Slavic *guja (“snake”), limited to South Slavic languages. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian гу́ја (“serpent”), гу̀јавица (“earthworm”).

parole.significato: granary weevil (pest beetle in genus Sitophilus, typically feeding on grain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gǫgrica, probably from Proto-Slavic *ǫgrъ (“vermin, serpent, creep”) + -ица (-ica) (with initial *g- similar to Bulgarian гъсени́ца (găseníca, “caterpillar”) from Proto-Slavic *ǫsěnica).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gъdьlъ /*gǫdьlъ (listed with a nasal vocalism in Gerov's dictionary).

parole.significato: cloth wound and tangled into a clump
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gǫži (jū-stem), later reanalyzed as an (v)a-stem.
From Proto-Slavic *gǫzъ/*guzъ. Slavic cognates include Serbo-Croatian guzica and Macedonian газ (gaz).

parole.significato: to bend, to twist, to fold

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *gъrdlica. Morphologically identical to гъ́рло (gắrlo, “throat”) + -ица (-ica).

parole.significato: to shoot, to fire (to produce a gunshot, usually with a firearm)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gǫsěnica, a variant of *ǫsěnica. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic юсеница (jusenica), Russian гу́сеница (gúsenica), Ukrainian гу́сениця (húsenycja), Serbo-Croatian гу̏сеница/gȕsenica/гу̏сјеница/gȕsjenica, Slovene gosẹ̑nica, Czech housenka, Slovak húsenica, Old Polish wąs

parole.significato: to thicken (to gradually become thick, dense, compact, or closely packed)

parole.testo: Unclear. Probably from an earlier *gǫčь, from Proto-Slavic *žęti (“to press, to squeeze”).

parole.significato: word used to indicate agreement or acceptance: yes

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *da (in the conjunction sense), related to the first etymology.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dāvàti (see there for further descendants). Morphologically parsable as дам (dam) + -вам (-vam).
Simplified from an earlier даждба (daždba), from Proto-Slavic *daďьba. Morphologically equivalent to Bulgarian дам (dam), да́да (dáda, “to give”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: far, far off (in space or time)
parole.testo: Adverbial equivalent of дале́чен (daléčen, “far, distant”), from Proto-Slavic *dalekъ.
From Proto-Slavic *dati, Proto-Balto-Slavic *dṓˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *dédeh₃ti (“to give”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *danьkъ. By surface analysis, дан (dan) + -ък (-ăk). Ultimately, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dṓˀnis, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃-.
From Proto-Slavic *darьba. Morphologically equivalent to дар (dar, “gift”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: to give, to gift, to present, to bestow (to give something as a gift, favour, honour, or benefit)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *darovati. By surface analysis, дар (dar) + -у́вам (-úvam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dъva desęti. By surface analysis, univerbation of два (dva) + де́сет (déset).
From Proto-Slavic *dvižimъ, the present passive participle of дви́жа (dvíža, “to move”) + -им (-im).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dvorьcь. By surface analysis, двор (dvor) + -ец (-ec)

parole.significato: thick, close-woven, heavy (of a material, fabric, etc.)
to get fat, to put on weight, to grow stout
to stalk, to lie in wait (for something or somebody), to be on the lookout for something, to be on the prowl, to shadow
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *debnǫti, cognate with Macedonian демне (demne)/дебне (debne). Written as дѣбнѫ (děbnǫ) in Gerov's dictionary (Vol. 1: 388), probably under the influence of the similar sounding Bulgarian дябам (djabam, “to seek advantage, to infiltrate”).

parole.significato: to prey, to hunt upon stealthily
parole.testo: Formally from Proto-Slavic *debiti (probably reanalyzed from Proto-Slavic *deběti), with no exact cognates in other Slavic languages. Probably akin to dialectal Serbo-Croatian дѐпсти (“to lie in wait, to ambush”), dialectal Russian дебе́ть (debétʹ, “to stand in one place”) (ě/i-conj.). According to
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *devęsilъ, literally "nine powers" (reflecting the plant's medicinal purposes).

parole.significato: to prevail, to defeat, to cope with
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *delěti, from Proto-Indo-European *delh₁- (“to split, to distribute”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *děliti (“to divide”). Synchronically, a causative-iterative of дял (djal, “share”).
From Proto-Slavic *dьnьsь, from *dьnь (“day”) + *sь; cognate with Macedonian денес (denes), Serbo-Croatian dànas, Slovene dánes.

parole.significato: to skin, to flay (to remove the skin, usually from a slaughtered animal)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьràti (“to tear, to flay”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *desnъ. In the modern language, the root vowel is interpreted as long *ě, probably due to influence from ляв (ljav, “left”) (< *lěvъ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dętelina. By surface analysis, де́тел (détel) + -и́на (-ína).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dětiťь. By surface analysis, дете́ (deté, “child”) + -ищ (-išt).

parole.significato: deed, act, action (something done by a person; an act or deed)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dějanьje. By surface analysis, де́я (déja) + -ние (-nie).

Attested in Southern Torlak dialects, cognate with Macedonian ѕрцки pl (dzrcki, “peepers”). According to Georgiev, possibly cognate with dialectal Russian згра (zgra), both from Proto-Slavic *stьdzrъ, *stьgrъ (“shining, sparkling”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teyg- (“to stick, to poke”).
