Uncertain. Per BER, native, perhaps inherited from Proto-Slavic *divъ (“some kind of evil spirit”) of further etymology unclear. Cognate with Old East Slavic дивъ (divŭ, “spirit”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *divakъ. By surface analysis, див (div, “wild”) + -ак (-ak).

parole.significato: wonderful, marvellous, splendid, magnificent (very beautiful, pleasant, impressive, or admirable)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *divьnъ. By surface analysis, див (div) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: wildstock, game (wild animals that are hunted for food or sport)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *divьjačь. By surface analysis, див (div, “wild”) + -еч (-eč).

parole.significato: wildness, savagery, untamedness (the quality or state of being wild, untamed, uncultivated, or not domesticated)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *divostь. By surface analysis, див (div) + -ост (-ost).

parole.significato: to drive wild, to make wild

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dvigati, with colloquial elision of *-v- after an alveolar (cf. *sъtvoriti → Bulgarian сторя (storja)).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dvignǫti. By surface analysis, ди́гам (dígam) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: giddy up, go (call to spur a harness animal (typically a horse or a donkey))
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *di. Functionally resembles an imperative 2p. form of unattested *diti. Compare synonymous Polish wio from Polish wiać (“to run, to flee”).

parole.significato: smoke (visible gas and particles produced by burning)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dyňa (from an earlier *kъdyňa, borrowed from Latin cydōnea).

parole.significato: crack, notch (remnant or result of tearing)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *diřa (given as *dyřa in Gerov's dictionary).

parole.significato: to look for, to seek, to explore
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *diriti. At least partially a causative-iterative of Etymology 1. Stang (followed by Derksen) tentatively considered a possible descend from a r-extension of Proto-Indo-European *deyH- (“to emit, to transcend?”), cognate with Lithuanian dyrė́ti (“to look out, to stare”),

parole.significato: to take a breath, to breathe (once)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dyxanьje, verbal noun of Bulgarian дихам (diham), from Proto-Slavic *dyxati (“to breathe”). Loaned into Romanian dihanie.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dyšati, a secondary form of *dyxnǫti + *-jati.

parole.significato: medical splint put against a fractured bone (to support its healing)
parole.testo: Most likely from Proto-Slavic *dolga. Georgiev (BER) tentatively proposes colloquial truncation of dialectal дла́бка (dlábka, “carved shape, notch”), classified as phonetically unlikely by Trubachev (ESSJa).

parole.significato: palm (of the hand), flat of the hand, thenar

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *delto, alternative form of *dolto, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dálbtan, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰelbʰ-.
From Proto-Slavic *dъlžьnъ, from *dъlgъ (“debt”) + *-ьnъ. Cognate with Macedonian должен (dolžen), Russian до́лжен (dólžen).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dobytъkъ. By surface analysis, доби́я (dobíja, “to extract, to acquire”) + -тък (-tăk). Cognate with Belarusian дабы́так (dabýtak), Macedonian добиток (dobitok), Polish dobytek, Serbo-Croatian доби́так, Ukrainian добу́ток (dobútok).

parole.significato: to acquire, to gain, to attain
to fight a little more, to finish up fighting
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dobiti; equivalent to до- (do-) + би́я (bíja, “to fight, to wrestle, to strike”).
From Proto-Slavic *dobľestь. Morphologically equivalent to до́бли (dóbli, “valiant, gallant”) (historical) + -ест (-est).

parole.significato: goodness, kindness, benevolence, good-heartedness (the quality of being good, kind, gentle, and well-disposed toward ot…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dobrota. By surface analysis, до́бър (dóbăr) + -ота (-ota)

parole.significato: good day (a greeting said in the daytime), good afternoon
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dòbrъ dь̏nь. By surface analysis, literally, “good day”.
From Proto-Slavic *dovьlěti (“to suffice”). Secondary meaning “to burden, to weigh on” has developed colloquially at a later time.

parole.significato: amount of milk from a single milking
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dojidlo. Equivalent to доя́ (dojá, “to milk”) + -ло (-lo).

From Proto-Slavic *dolъ. Typically reconstructed as an o-stem, in Bulgarian the word exhibits u-stem declension, as attested in the adverb Bulgarian до́лу (dólu, “down”) (fosilized locative case). Compare Old Church Slavonic долъ (dolŭ), gen. долоу (dolu).

Fossilized locative singular of Proto-Slavic *dolъ (“valley”) (u-stem in Old Church Slavonic and Bulgarian). Compare го́ре (góre, “up”), originally "to/on the mountain", and note the semantic parallels with English down, originally "from the hill" (compare dialectal English down (“hill”) and English

parole.significato: homebody, stay-at-home (a person who prefers to stay at home and avoids going out, travelling, or socialising much)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *domasědъ. By surface analysis, дом (dom) + -о- (-o-) + седя́ (sedjá). Literally, “home-sitter”.

parole.significato: annoyance, irritation, vexation (a feeling of displeasure, irritation, or dissatisfaction caused by something unpleasan…

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *do sъta. Compare Russian доста́ть (dostátʹ, “to be enough (dated)”), Serbo-Croatian достати (“to be enough”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dostatъkъ. By surface analysis, до́ста (dósta, “plenty”) + -тък (-tăk).
From Proto-Slavic *dostižimъ, a present passive participle of Proto-Slavic *dostižiti + -им (-im), the causative variant of Bulgarian дости́гам (dostígam, “to reach”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dostojьnъ. Compare сто́йност (stójnost, “cost, worth”), Russian сто́ить (stóitʹ, “to be worth”).

parole.significato: to reach, to reach out (for), to touch (someone or something)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *doxodъ. Compare Russian дохо́д (doxód).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dorga (“road”), related to Bulgarian дъ́рзам (dắrzam, “to stretch, to comb”) (dialectal).
From Proto-Slavic *dorgyni; equivalent to драг (drag, “dear”) + -иня (-inja). Indirectly attested in the derivative Bulgarian драги́нко (dragínko, “best man”).

parole.significato: dearness, belovedness, preciousness (the quality of being dear, beloved, or precious to someone)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dorgostь. By surface analysis, драг (drag) + -ост (-ost).

parole.significato: to tease, to provoke (a person or animal)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *draskati. By surface analysis, дра́пам (drápam, “to scrape”) + -скам (-skam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *draščiti. From the same root as дра́скам (dráskam).

parole.significato: trifle, bagatelle (tiny, insignificant detail or nuance)
parole.testo: From an obsolete дре́боля (drébolja, “to shred, to shatter, to gut”) + -ия (-ija). Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *drebъ.

parole.significato: antiquity, ancientness (the quality or state of being ancient, very old, or belonging to remote times)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *drevьnostь. By surface analysis, дре́вен (dréven) + -ост (-ost)
From Proto-Slavic *drybati (“to crumple”) + -ак (-ak). Attested in the Rhodope region and Thrace. Perhaps the same as synonymous дръмба́к (drămbák, “thicket, clump”)?
From Proto-Slavic *drika (“shaft, cart”). Possibly akin to Romanian dric (“cart”), although the later is considered a Hungarian loanword.

parole.significato: to have diarrhea, to shit (of a person or animal, to excrete frequent and watery feces)
yeast (unicellular microorganisms that cause fermentation of sugars)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *drozdъ, *drozgъ. Akin to English thrush.

parole.significato: bustard (bird of family Otidae), in particular great bustard (Otis tarda)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dropľа, *dropy, probably a back-formation of Proto-Slavic *dьropъty (“fleeing bird”).

parole.significato: to stroll, to go back and forth
to be friends, to associate, to keep company (to be in relations of friendship or companionship with someone)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *družьba. Morphologically equivalent to друг (drug, “other, fellow”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: company, band, group, troop, retinue (a group of people united by companionship, common action, service, or leadership)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *drъgnǫti. Semantically influenced by Proto-Slavic *dьrgnǫti.

parole.significato: to dare, to have the courage (to do something)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *drъmъ, a m-extension from the root of дърво́ (dărvó, “tree”). Compare Ancient Greek δρῡμός (drūmós, “grove, wood”).

parole.significato: to pull, to drag, to tug
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьrpnǫti, with metathesis swapping the position of the ъ and р.

parole.significato: to say, to speak, to talk (to utter words; to speak or say something)
to blow, to gust (to create air current)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *duxati. By surface analysis, дух (duh) + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: to blow (of wind or air: to begin to blow)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *duxnǫti. By surface analysis, ду́хам (dúham) + -на (-na)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *duxovъ. By surface analysis, дух (duh, “spirit, gasp”) + -ов (-ov).

parole.significato: witty, humorous, clever, facetious (able to express humour, cleverness, or quick intelligence in speech or writing)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *duxovitъ. By surface analysis, дух (duh) + -овит (-ovit).

parole.significato: to strangle, to choke (to squeeze someone’s throat so as to prevent breathing)
to sniff, to smell, to scent (to draw in air through the nose in order to perceive or follow a smell)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dušьnъ. By surface analysis, душа́ (dušá) + -ен (-en).
From Proto-Slavic *dǫbъ, via Old Church Slavonic дѫбъ (dǫbŭ).

parole.significato: rainbow (a multicoloured arch in the sky, produced by prismatic refraction of light within droplets of rain in the air)
drizzle, shower (a small, light, or gentle rain)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dъždžьcь. By surface analysis, дъжд (dăžd) + -ец (-ec)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dъždžiti. Synchronically, a denominative causative of дъжд (dăžd, “rain”).

parole.significato: to carve, to delve, to hollow
groove, socket, concave slot (where another part fits into)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dьlbьjь or *dьlbějь. Equivalent to дълба́я (dălbája, “to delve”) + -ей (-ej).
From earlier *dlǫbokъ which arose from the contamination of Proto-Slavic *glǫbokъ with *dъlbokъ.

parole.significato: debt (state or condition of owing something to another)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьlžina, from *dьlgъ (“long”) + *-ina. By surface analysis, дъ́лъг (dắlăg) + -ина (-ina).

parole.significato: bottom, bed (of a body of water, valley, pit, trench)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dъno (“bottom”), equivalent to *dъb- + -но (-no). From the same stem is де́бър (débăr, “depression, interior of a forest”).
From Proto-Slavic *drъvьje (“trees”), originally meaning cluster of trees. Morphologically, equivalent to дърво́ (dărvó, “tree”) + -е (-e).

parole.significato: to scutch, to flog (seeds from plants)
parole.testo: Mix-up of Proto-Slavic *drъgati (“to shake, to quiver”) and Proto-Slavic *dьrgati ~ *dьrdzati (“to pluck”) (which principally yields Bulgarian дъ́рзам (dắrzam, “to scutch”)).

parole.significato: to hold, to have a grip of
to hold one's tongue, to keep quiet, to keep one's mouth shut (to refrain from speaking, especially in order not to rev…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьržati ęzykъ za zǫby. Literally, “to keep [my] tongue behind [my] teeth”.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьrdzati, an alternative form of Proto-Slavic *dьrgati via third palatalization (*-g- > *-dz- > Bulg. -z- after accented *-ь-).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьrzъkъ. Synchronically parsable as (archaic) дръз (drăz) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to pull, to drag, to tug
to age, to become old or decrepit (to become old, losing youthful appearance, strength, or vitality)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *dьrcati, an alternative form of Proto-Slavic *dьrkati via third palatalization (*-k- > *-c- before *ь). Compare Bulgarian дързам (dărzam) (reflecting Proto-Slavic *dьrdzati) from Proto-Slavic *dьrgati.

parole.significato: bad weather (with rain and high wind)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьrča, limited to South Slavic.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dъxavъ. By surface analysis, дъх (dăh, “inhaling”) + -ав (-av).
From earlier ду́ля (dúlja), гду́ля (gdúlja) and гду́ня (gdúnja), from Proto-Slavic *kъduňa, from Latin cydōnia, from Ancient Greek Κυδωνία (Kudōnía, “quince-tree”).

Formally from an earlier Proto-Slavic *děbati (probably originally a/j-conj.), from the same origin as Old Church Slavonic оудѣбенъ (uděbenŭ, “overtaken, caught by surprise”). According to Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary, related to dialectal Bulgarian дебя (debja, “to pray upon, to sneak”). On th
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *děvati. By surface analysis, дя́на (djána) + -вам (-vam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dělati. Superseded in the contemporary language by Etymology 1.

From Proto-Slavic *dělьba. Morphologically equivalent to дял (djal, “share”) + -ба (-ba). Doublet of делба́ (delbá), a dialectal variant spread from Western dialects, which is more frequently attested.

parole.significato: used to express indignation, dissatisfaction, irritation, annoyance
to joke, to make a joke
to bristle, to stand on end (of hair, fur, feathers, etc.: to stand upright)
ride (on a horse or other animal)
lake, lacustrine (relating to a lake or lakes)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ezerьnъ. By surface analysis, е́зеро (ézero) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: tongue (the flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into v…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ęzykъ, from Early Proto-Slavic *inzū́kus, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *inźūˀ-kas (perhaps directly linked to the non-standard variant е́нзик), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *inźūˀs, from earlier *dinźūˀs, from Proto-Indo-European *dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s.

parole.significato: fir tree (conifer tree of genus Abies)
alder (deciduous tree or shrub of genus Alnus, within the birch family Betulaceae)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)elьšа, a ja-stem variant of *olьxa ~ *elьxa.

parole.significato: autumn, fall, autumnal (occurring in, belonging to, characteristic of, or done during the season of autumn)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *esenьnъ. By surface analysis, е́сен (ésen) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to resound, to echo, to reverberate (to sound loudly and continuously, spreading far)
barley (cereal of the species Hordeum vulgare, or its grains)
to crave, to yearn, to long for, to dream about
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *žęděti (ě/i-conj.), parallel to synonymous Bulgarian жаду́вам (žadúvam), же́дам (žédam). In some dialects levelled out as pure i-conjugation (as if from *žęďiti).
From Proto-Slavic *žalьba. Morphologically equivalent to жал (žal, “sorrow, grief”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: to feel sorrow, grief, or pity for something or someone; to grieve, to mourn
to mourn, to grieve, to sorrow (for someone or something)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *žarъkъ, morphologically formed as жар (žar, “heat, glow”) + -ък (-ăk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *žàriti. By surface analysis, жар (žar) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to chew, to masticate (to chew food, gum, tobacco, etc., especially slowly, noisily, or repeatedly)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *žьvakati. By surface analysis, (obsolete) жва (žva, “to chew”) + -кам (-kam) (from Proto-Slavic *žьvati).
By surface analysis, (obsolete) жва (žva, “to chew”) + -ча (-ča) (from Proto-Slavic *žьvati).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *žežьkъ. By surface analysis, жежа́ (žežá, “to heat up”) + -ък (-ăk). Akin to Russian жгу́чий (žgúčij, “scorching”).
From Proto-Slavic *žezlъ, possibly reinforced by Russian жезл (žezl).
Deverbal noun from жела́я (želája, “to wish, to desire”) + -ние (-nie), from Proto-Slavic *želati.

parole.significato: to wish, to desire, to long for

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *želьba (“wish”). Morphologically equivalent to жела́я (želája, “to wish”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: stomach (the internal organ in which food is digested after passing from the oesophagus)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ženixъ. Agent noun of же́ня се (žénja se, “to get a wife”) + -их (-ih).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ženьskъ. Equivalent to жена́ (žená, “woman”) + -ски (-ski).
Blend of Proto-Slavic *žeravľь (soft declension) and Proto-Slavic *žeravъ (hard declension).
From Proto-Slavic *žerava, a substantivized form of Proto-Slavic *žeravъ (“burning, scorching”).
From an earlier *жернка (*žernka), a diminutive form of Proto-Slavic *žьrny (“millstone”) + -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: cruel, brutal, merciless, mean, obdurate, implacable, inexorable, relentless, atrocious, monstrous, outrageous

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *živěti. By surface analysis, жив (živ) + -ея (-eja).

parole.significato: liveliness, vivacity, animation, vitality (the quality of being lively, animated, energetic, or full of life)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *živostь. By surface analysis, жи́в (žív) + -ост (-ost)
From Proto-Slavic *žilavъ. Morphologically equivalent to жи́ла (žíla, “sinew”) + -ав (-av).

parole.significato: to sting, to bite (of insects, vermins, nettle)
hagiography, saint's life, life of a saint (a narrative about the life, deeds, miracles, sufferings, or martyrdom of a…
wire, cable (flexible metal thread, used primarily as an electrical conductor)
gland (organ that produces or filters hormones, secrets, and galls)

parole.testo: From жребе́ц (žrebéc, “stallion”) + -е (-e, diminutive suffix). Displaced an earlier жребе́ (žrebé) from Proto-Slavic *žerbę.
From Proto-Slavic *žerdlo. Formed from the nowadays obsolete жра (žra, “to gobble”) + -ло (-lo, “instrumental suffix”).

parole.significato: to hum, to buzz, to drone (of insects)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *žužati. Onomatopoeic. Compare Russian жужжа́ть (žužžátʹ).

parole.significato: cicada (hemipteran insect of family Cicadoidea, known for their hissing songs during summer)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *žužeľь, of onomatopoeic origin. Derived from жу́жа (žúža, “to hum”) + -ел (-el).

parole.significato: to scour, to scrub, to chafe
to squint, to narrow one's eyes (to close or partly close the eyes, usually because of strong light)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *žętva. Doublet of жетва (žetva).

parole.significato: used to indicate the place someone or something is going to or toward; for, to
amusement, diversion, distraction, pastime, merry-making, fun

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zabavьnъ, a relational adjective from заба́ва (zabáva, “amusement”) + -ен (-en).
From заби́я (zabíja, “to slam”) + -тък (-tăk), from an earlier Proto-Slavic *zabitъkъ.

parole.significato: delusion, misconception (an incorrect belief or idea resulting from misunderstanding, lack of knowledge, or false assum…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zablǫda. By surface analysis, deverbal from заблудя (zabludja).

parole.significato: to find, to come upon, to meet (to find someone or something somewhere, usually upon arriving)

parole.testo: за́вря pf (závrja, “to tumult, to wail”) (dialectal, obsolescent) + -ушка (-uška) (from Proto-Slavic *vьrati (“to lament, to groan”))

parole.significato: to thrust, to poke, to stick, to stuff, to shove, to squeeze, to ram, to tuck

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zaduxъ. By surface analysis, за- (za-) + дух (duh).
From Proto-Slavic *zajęcь. Dialectally, also encountered as зо́як (zójak), зо́ек (zóek), зàец (zàec), зȃк (zȃk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zaęti. Equivalent to за- (za-) + -е́ма (-éma).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zakana; equivalent to за- (za-) + ка́я се (kája se, “to regret, to repent one’s sins”) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: any of several shrubs of the genus Cytisus, broom
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zanovětь, reanalyzed with the diminutive suffix -ец (-ec).

parole.significato: binge, bender, bout (a period of heavy and continuous drinking, especially of alcohol)
attachment, seizure, garnishment (a legal restriction prohibiting someone from disposing of money, bank deposits, prope…
to harness, to yoke, to hitch an animal to a cart, plough, sledge, etc.

parole.testo: From запра́ (zaprá, “to obstruct, to hinder”) + -тък (-tăk), from an earlier Proto-Slavic *zapъrtъkъ.

parole.significato: shelter, cover, refuge (a place or light structure giving protection from bad weather, danger, or exposure)
merit, desert, worthiness (the quality of deserving praise, reward, recognition, or respect because of one’s actions or…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zasluga. By surface analysis, за- (za-) + слу́га (slúga).

parole.significato: to deserve, to merit, to rate, to be worthy, to be worth, to earn

parole.testo: From за- (za-) + Proto-Slavic *ustra (“dawn”) (compare Old Church Slavonic заоустра (zaustra), attested in Ps. sin.). Doublet of у́тро (útro) (the later levelled out from *jutro (“early, soon”)).

By surface analysis, за- (za-) + *тна (*tna). Diachronically, probably from Proto-Slavic *zatęti (“to strike down”) (pres. stem: *zatьnǫ)? Bulgarian Etymology Dictionary derives the semantics from formally unrelated затъ́кна (zatắkna, “to thrust into”).
Formally reflects an earlier *zatьra, a deverbal noun from Proto-Slavic *zaterti (“to scratch, to rub off”).
From заче́на (začéna, “to begot”) + -тък (-tăk), from an earlier Proto-Slavic *začętъkъ. Cognate with Russian зача́ток (začátok).

parole.significato: to become pregnant with (young), to conceive (offspring), to beget, to procreate
to begin to read, to start reading
to shield, to protect, to defend

parole.testo: Fossilized past perfect participle of Bulgarian защитя́ (zaštitjá, “to shield”), from Proto-Slavic *zaščitenъ.

parole.significato: to shield, to protect, to defend

parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *zveno, but the exact course of descent is disputed: * Borrowed from Russian звено́ (zvenó), at least for the standard meanings; * Possibly inherited, as evident by doublets such as dialectal звъна́ f (zvăná), дзво́но (dzvóno, “piece, bit, slip”).
Reanalysed plurale tantum of Proto-Slavic *zveno sg, interpreted as a feminine a-stem. Effectively, a doublet of звено́ (zvenó) (Russian loanword).

parole.significato: to ring, to jingle, to clink, to chime (to emit a ringing sound, of metal objects, bells, or the sound itself)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *sъdorvьje. Morphologically equivalent to здрав (zdrav, “healthy”) + -е (-e).

parole.significato: crack, fissure, opening, aperture, gap (a crack, opening, hole, or aperture)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zěvъ, related to зе́я (zéja).

parole.significato: cabbage (plant of varieties of species Brassica oleracea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *zelьje (“foliage”), originally a collective sg. tantum with meaning cluster of greenery, leaves. Morphologically equivalent to Proto-Slavic *zelь + -е (-e).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zemьnъ. By surface analysis, земя́ (zemjá) + -ен (-en), and/or Земя́ (Zemjá) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to gape (to stand wide open or exposed, especially of a door, grave, wound, hole, gap, etc.)
to mason, to lay bricks or stones, to build a wall

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zidařь. By surface analysis, зи́дам (zídam, “to build”) + -ар (-ar).

parole.significato: to open one's mouth, to gape, to open wide (to open the mouth wide, especially from surprise, fear, hunger, or in order…
malice, spite, ill will, malevolence (a hostile, malicious, or spiteful feeling toward someone; desire to harm or see s…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zъloba. By surface analysis, зъл (zăl) + -оба (-oba).
From Proto-Slavic *zъlobivъ. Formed from злобя́ (zlobjá, “to cause malice”) + -ив (-iv).

From Proto-Slavic *zmьjь. The meaning dragon is likely secondary, evolved from an earlier snake, reptile or more generally a creature that dwells on the ground. From the same root as Bulgarian земя́ (zemjá, “earth, ground”) (е-grade), derived through 0-grade ablaut and the suffix -ей (-ej).
From Proto-Slavic *znamę. Parsable as зна́я (znája, “to know”) + -ме (-me).

parole.significato: omen, portent (an unusual phenomenon, usually natural, interpreted as a sign foretelling exceptional or fateful events)
folk healer, medicine man (a person who treats illness by folk remedies, herbs, charms, prayers, or traditional practic…

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *značiti. By surface analysis, знак (znak) + -а (-a).

parole.significato: to know (be certain or sure about (something))

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *znojь. Probably a doublet of гной (gnoj).

parole.significato: to consume, to guzzle up (for animals)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zobati (a-conj). By surface analysis, зоб (zob, “fodder, nutrient”) + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: to feed, to provide fodder (to animals)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zobiti, denominal causative of *zobь (“fodder”). Morphologically, a doublet of Etymology 1.
Deverbal from зова́ (zová, “to evoke”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *zovъ.

parole.significato: to call, to summon (to call someone to come; to invite or urge someone to appear)
to write, to inscribe, to draw
parole.testo: According to Bulgarian Etymological Dicitonary, from Proto-Slavic *zьdati (“to build”) (whence standard Bulgarian зи́дам (zídam, “to mason”)) with dialectal widening of the yer *-ь- > -o-. Compare also Lithuanian žãdas (“speech, pledge”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zorъkъ. By surface analysis, зор (zor, “sight, view”) (dated) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to light up, to break (of dawn)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zoriti, a causative-iterative of зора́ (zorá, “dawn”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to see, to look at, to gaze

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *zьriteľь; equivalent to зра (zra, “to watch, look at”) + -тел (-tel, “er”).
From Proto-Slavic *zujьkъ (“drizzle, buzz”), possibly of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Bulgarian жуже́не (žužéne, “buzzing”). Cognate with Russian зуёк (zujók, “plover”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zǫbatъ. By surface analysis, зъб (zăb, “tooth”) + -ат (-at).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zьrcadlo. Synchronically analyzable as dial. зъ́рчам (zắrčam), зерца́я (zercája, “to peek”) + -ало (-alo).

parole.significato: to agape (one's mouth, а valve, an outlet)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zěpati (“to gape”). Meaning “to stare, to observe with amaze” may also reflect a contraction of an earlier *заяпам from Proto-Slavic *za(j)apati (“to observe”).

parole.significato: and (used to connect two homogeneous similar words or phrases)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьgъla, equivalent to иго (igo, “yoke”) + -ла (-la).

parole.significato: primrose (any flower of the genus Primula)
parole.testo: Origin disputed; possibly via игла́ (iglá, “needle”), although spurious, due to theorized inheritance from Proto-Slavic *jagla (“grain”) in ягли́ка and subsequent reduction to егли́ка and ultimately игли́ка; cognates of ягли́ка include Serbo-Croatian јаглика, whereas parallels of агли́ка are drawn i
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati. By surface analysis, игра (igra, “game”) + -а́я (-ája).
From Proto-Slavic *jьgrivъ. Formed as игра́ (igrá, “game, play”) + -ив (-iv).

parole.significato: to go, to proceed, to change position
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьti. A unique characteristic of this verb is that, unlike other cognates, the l-participle stem was regularized from a stem *и́д- (*íd-), used in the present tense and similar forms, instead of being derived from Proto-Slavic *šьd- (cf. Polish szedłem (I went), Russian

parole.significato: to beat, to pound, to knock off
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьzbiti; equivalent to из- (iz-) + бия (bija, “to beat, to fight, to wrestle”).

parole.significato: to erupt, to burst, to surge out (for material, force)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьzbyti, related to Bulgarian избу́я (izbúja, “to thrive, to bloom out”).
From из- (iz-) + Proto-Slavic *bǫdnǫti. Borrowed into Romanian izbândi (“to overcome”).

parole.significato: spring (place where water or another liquid flows to the surface)
sunrise (appearance of the sun in the morning)
unnecessary, needless, superfluous (not necessary, needed, or useful in a particular situation)
parole.testo: By surface analysis, из- (iz-) + лих (lih) + -ен (-en), from Proto-Slavic *lixъ (“remaining, unnecessary, superfluous, bad”).

parole.significato: deceit, deception, circumvention, dupery, foul play, guile, double-dealing, cheating, suck-in, take-in, cozenage, flimf…

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьz nenada. By surface analysis, из- (iz-) + не- (ne-) + на́да (náda, “thread, effect, result”) (obsolete)

parole.significato: to depict, to portray, to represent (visually)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьzportiti; equivalent to из- (iz-) + пра́тя (prátja).

parole.significato: to overtake, to pass (while moving, to go ahead of someone or something moving in the same direction)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьzrazъ (“cut-off”), deverbative of archaic изразити (izraziti, “to frame, to mould (by cutting)”). Parallel to northern Proto-Slavic *vyrazъ (with prefix *vy- (“out of”)).

parole.significato: to express, to convey, to articulate
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьzraziti. By surface analysis, из- (iz-) + разя́ (razjá).

parole.significato: to pronounce, to utter, to say, to speak
to read (all, to the end), to read through

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьlъ, *jilъ. Attested more in Western dialects.

parole.significato: mistletoe (parasitic evergreen plant of genus Viscum)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jemèlъ, via a semi-regular reduction of unaccented e- > ь- (compare Old Church Slavonic мьнѣ (mĭně) < *meně̀ for a similar diachronic change).

parole.significato: to name, to call, to designate
otherwise, else (in a different manner; differently)
not this sort of, not this type of, not this kind of, not like this, different, other (not of the type already mentione…
sincere, frank, candid, unaffected, honest, outspoken, straightforward, genuine, real, heartfelt, deepfelt
to sparkle, to spark (to emit or throw off sparks)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jьskriti. By surface analysis, искра́ (iskrá, “spark”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to throw, to bash something (furiously, like a lightning)
to poop, to defecate (to pass feces; used especially in child-directed or informal speech)
what, what kind of, what sort of, what type of (used to ask for a description)
guelder rose, viburnum, Viburnum opulus (a shrub with white flowers and bright red berries)
to temper (metal, glass, etc.), to harden
to muddy (to make something dirty by covering it with mud)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kamenica, morphologically equivalent to камен (kamen, “stone”) (poetic, dated) + -ица (-ica), with unclear stress shift.
From Proto-Slavic *kamenьje (“gravel”), originally meaning cluster of stones, rocks. Morphologically, equivalent to ка́мен (kámen, “stone”) (dated) + -е (-e).
From Proto-Slavic *kaňa, probably of onomatopoeic origin akin to Bulgarian ча́йка (čájka, “seagull”). Compare English hen, French canard (“drake”), all from Proto-Indo-European *kan- (“to sing”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kaniti. Cognate with Macedonian кани (kani, “to invite”), Serbo-Croatian ка́нити (“to intend”), Slovene kanīti/kániti (“to agitate”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kapъka. By surface analysis, ка́пя (kápja) + -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: to drip, to drop, to fall as a drop (of a liquid: to fall in a drop or drops)
to drip, to dribble, to trickle

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *karati (“to accuse”), an iterative counter-part to коря́ (korjá, “to rebuke”).

parole.significato: to touch, to affect, to concern
parole.testo: Factitive-iterative of obsolete ко́сна (kósna, “to touch, to affect”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *kasati, with literary sense reinforced at a later time by Russian каса́ться (kasátʹsja).

parole.significato: to span, to wind, to unwrap
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *katati, with some meanings borrowed from Russian ката́ться (katátʹsja) (from the same origin).

From Proto-Slavic *kačьka, either onomatopoeic or expressive. Equivalent to ка́чам (káčam, “to swindle”) (colloquial) + -ка (-ka). In other Slavic languages means duck, e.g. Polish kaczka, Czech kačka, Russian ка́чка (káčka), Ukrainian ка́чка (káčka).

parole.significato: to cough (to noisily expel air from the lungs due to irritation)
to repent, to lament, to experience regret
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kajati sę, a reflexive derivative from an obsolete ка́я (kája, “to incite, to instigate regret”) (in other Slavic languages: to reprimand, to reproach).

parole.significato: leaven, yeast, barm (a catalyst that causes fermentation)
to ferment, to culture, to make yogurt (to add starter culture to fresh milk so that it ferments)
prong, tine (pointy tip of a weapon or a tool)
to boil (to bubble because of being heated)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kysělъ, from an earlier *kypsělъ or from *kytsělъ.

parole.significato: to adorn, to decorate, to embellish (someone or something)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kyxati, of imitative origin.

parole.significato: to adorn, to decorate, to deck (someone or something with flowers, jewelry, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kyčiti, derived from *kyta (whence Bulgarian ки́тка (kítka)).

Of onomatopoeic origin, similar to Bulgarian бълбу́к (bălbúk, “sound of bubbling water”). Formally reflects Proto-Slavic *kolbukъ (with stem probably related to Russian колоб (kolob, “sphere, ball”)).

parole.significato: to stack, to pile, to put together
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *klasti. Some dictionaries distinguish the meanings “to pile, to stack” from “to make fire, to kindle”

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kolda. Doublet of коло́да (kolóda) (Russian borrowing). Because of their close meanings and their identical form, this sense is sometimes considered an alternative meaning of Etymology 2. The two, however, are etymologically unrelated.

parole.significato: to wag, to swing, to rock
slander, calumny, defamation (a false accusation or lie intended to discredit, blacken, or harm someone’s reputation)
to slander, to defame, to libel

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *klějь / *kъlějь. Dialectal doublet forms reflect *klьjь / *kъlьjь.

parole.significato: mountain pine (conifer shrub of species Pinus mugo)
maple, maple tree (tree of genus Acer)
to open and close some aperture repeatedly (e.g. of a brass instrument)
parole.testo: Probably derived from Proto-Slavic *klepati (“to clap, to smack”) via semantic shift.

parole.significato: to clang, to rap, to chime (to make noise by hitting something)
parole.testo: Via a merger of Proto-Slavic *klepati (“to clap”) and *klępati (“to distort”).
* According to BER: of onomatopoeic origin. * According to ESSJa: ultimately a factitive from Proto-Slavic *klěvъ (“crooked”).

parole.significato: simple footwear: sandal, slipper, house shoe
parole.testo: Either: * From an earlier кле́пка (klépka), a diminutive of Proto-Slavic *klępa (“snare, noose”) + -ка (-ka); * Formed on a native soil from кле́фам (kléfam, “to stroll”) or perhaps кле́пя (klépja, “to wear out”).

parole.significato: to squat, to crouch (to stand with bent knees without the body touching the ground)
to resound, to resonate, to clang, to ring
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *klikati. Morphologically equivalent to клик (klik) + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: to simmer, to bubble (to boil gently)
to incline, to lean, to tend toward a direction (of the sun, a road, a path, etc.: to be directed or move toward some s…

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *klękati, with root vocalism influenced by semantically related ся́дам (sjádam, “to sit”) < *sědati.

parole.significato: to make noise while walking with big shoes (like slippers or boots)
parole.testo: Formally from an earlier *klěpati, an intensive variant (vṛddhi) of Proto-Slavic *klepati (“to slap”).

From Proto-Slavic *koba, an alternative form of Proto-Slavic *kobь, whence Old Church Slavonic кобь (kobĭ, “destiny”). BER further relates it with dialectal кобе́ц (kobéc, “sparrowhawk”), presumingly of expressive origin.
From Proto-Slavic *kobьcь (“small bird of prey”). Akin to English hawk.

parole.significato: to forge, to hammer, to smith, to beat into shape (to strike heated metal with a hammer in order to shape it or make an…
treacherous, perfidious, deceitful (acting with hidden malice, betrayal, or dishonesty)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kovačь. By surface analysis, кова́ (ková, “to hew”) + -ач (-ač)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kovъkъ. By surface analysis, ко́ва (kóva, “to hew, forge”) + -ък (-ăk).
From Proto-Slavic *kozьlъ. Morphologically equivalent to коза́ (kozá, “goat”) + -ел (-el).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kozьjь. By surface analysis, коза́ (kozá) + -и (-i).
Reanalyzed plural of Proto-Slavic *kolo n (“wheel”), reinterpreted as а feminine singular.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kolařь. By surface analysis, кола́ (kolá, “cart”) + -а́р (-ár)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kolačь. By surface analysis, ко́ло (kólo, “wheel”) + -ач (-ač).

wheel, wheeled (relating to a wheel or wheels)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kolivo. Most likely from ко́ля (kólja, “to slaughter”) + -иво (-ivo). Sometimes viewed as another meaning of Etymology 2.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kolovozъ (“rut, wheel track”). Surface analysis can be done as кола́ (kolá, “wheel, cart”) and во́зя (vózja, “to transport”)
From Proto-Slavic *komarъ, of onomatopoeic origin. By surface analysis, *ком- (*kom-, “humming”) + -ар (-ar).

parole.significato: sweet clover, melilot (flower of genus Melilotus)
horse, equine (relating to a horse or horses)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *konьnъ. By surface analysis, кон (kon) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: horseman (a man who rides a horse)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *konьnikъ. By surface analysis, кон (kon) + -ник (-nik).

parole.significato: cavalry (a branch of the army consisting of soldiers who fight or move on horseback)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *konьnica. By surface analysis, кон (kon) + -ница (-nica)

parole.significato: horse, equine (relating to a horse or horses)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *konьskъ. By surface analysis, кон (kon) + -ски (-ski)
From Proto-Slavic *kopaňa, morphologically from копа́я (kopája, “to dig, to ditch”) + -аня (-anja).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopьnъ (n-stem noun). By surface analysis, ко́па (kópa, “heap”) + -ен (-en, “nominal”).

parole.significato: snowless, not covered in snow (where snow has melted)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopьnъ (in-stem adjective). Cognate to Slovene kópən, kópenski (“dry (of land)”).
From Proto-Slavic *kopьje (“stabber”), originally a substantivation of a deverbal adjective from копа́я (kopája, “to dig”) + -ие (-ie).

parole.significato: to melt in parts (for snow, ice)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopьněti. Synchronically, related to adjective ко́пен (kópen, “snowless”).

parole.significato: to form a heap, to pile up, to stack
parole.testo: Causative-iterative of копа́ (kopá, “heap”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopiti.
Merger of Proto-Slavic *korabъ (о-stem) and *korabľь (jo-stem) ~ *korabь (i-stem), of Ancient Greek origin.

From Proto-Slavic *koristь, originally meaning loot, award (from a conquest). Compare Old Church Slavonic користь (koristĭ, “loot, booty, award”). parole.significato: self-interested, mercenary, self-seeking, greedy (guided by personal gain, profit, or selfish interest)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *koristьnъ. By surface analysis, ко́рист (kórist) + -ен (-en)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kosъ, possibly from an earlier *kopsъ (probably meaning pecker). See also Bulgarian кобе́ц (kobéc, “hawk”).

parole.significato: hair (the collection or mass of filaments growing from the skin of humans and animals)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kosatъ (“haired”). By surface analysis, коса́ (kosá, “hair”) (collective) + -ат (-at).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kosatъ (“fin”). By surface analysis, коса́ (kosá, “scythe”) + -ат (-at).

parole.significato: indirect, roundabout, mediate (not direct; done, expressed, or reaching something through an intermediate person, thing…
bone, bony, osseous (relating to bone or bones)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kostьnъ. By surface analysis, кост (kost) + -ен (-en)

parole.significato: perch, bass (freshwater fish of family Percidae)
parole.testo: In view of alternative forms, probably secondary from adjective Proto-Slavic *kostrъ /*kostьrъ (“prickly, bristly”), possibly cognate with Etymologies 2 and 3. Akin to Russian кoстёр (kostjór, “type of sturgeon”). Compare typologically Proto-Germanic *barsaz (whence English bass, barse) < Proto-Indo
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kosturъ. By surface analysis, кост (kost, “bone”) + -ур (-ur).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kotъ (“cat”), a wanderwort of unclear origin.

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kotъ (“type of framework”), of native origin.

parole.significato: corner, niche within some area or а room
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kotarъ, possibly from *kotiti (“to roll, to span”) + -ар (-ar). Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary tentatively compares it with Latin catēna (“chain”), whence loanword Bulgarian катина́р (katinár, “padlock”).

parole.significato: loop, curl, twine (of socks or stockings)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kotelь. By surface analysis, (obsolete) *кот (*kot, “entanglement”) + -ел (-el).

parole.significato: to bear, to brood, to give birth to

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *košuľa, from Vulgar Latin casula (“cloak”).

parole.significato: hind, doe (female deer, a mammal of order Artiodactyla)
foxtail, bristle grass (herb of genus Setaria)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kostrъ /*kostьrъ (“prickly, bristly”) + -ява (-java) with regular palatalization of the whole cluster -стр- + -j- > -штр-.

parole.significato: to please, to satisfy child's desires
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kojiti (“to heed”), cognate with Polish koić, Slovak kojiť. Attested mainly with pejorative sense to heed, to soothe > to please one's desires in its perfective form *коя̀вам > куѐвам (with dialectal reduction of unaccented median *-o- > -у-). In other Slavic languages, the same v

parole.significato: kravai, korovai (circle-shaped bread with a hole in the middle, used for rituals and celebrations)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *korgujь, *korguľь, cognate with Serbo-Croatian кра̀гӯј, крагу́јац, Slovene kragúlj, dialectal Ukrainian крагу́й (krahúj), кря́гулець (krjáhulecʹ), крогуле́ць (krohulécʹ) (probably borrowed from Polish), Polish krogulec, Czech krahujec, Slovak krahulec. From an earlier краждба (kraždba), from Proto-Slavic *kraďьba. Morphologically equivalent to крада́ (kradá, “to steal”) + -ба (-ba).
From Proto-Slavic *korpъ, either a wanderwort of pre-Slavic origin (cf. Latin carpa) or substantivized from the root of Proto-Slavic *korpavъ (“rough, scrubby”).

parole.significato: beautiful, lovely, fair, well-favoured, handsome, good-looking, fine-looking
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krasivъ. Formed from крася́ (krasjá, “to adorn”) + -ив (-iv).

parole.significato: paint, pigment, dye (a substance used to colour, paint, dye, or cover a surface)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *korstavъ. Morphologically equivalent to кра́ста (krásta, “scab”) + -ав (-av). Cognate with Macedonian крастав (krastav).
By surface analysis, крак (krak) + -ка (-ka), from Proto-Slavic *korkъ.

parole.significato: to move with difficulties, to trudge, to drag

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krěpъkъ. Formed from an earlier крѣпъ (krěp) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to support, to uphold, to sustain
to trudge, to tramp with heavy steps (due to exhaustion or encountered hindrance)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krěxъkъ. Formed from an earlier крѣхъ (krěh) + -ък (-ăk). Cognate with Czech křehký.

parole.significato: to shout, to scream, to yell, to cry
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krěščati (cf. Serbo-Croatian крије́штати) or *kręščati (Gerov), of onomatopoeic origin. By surface analysis, кря́сък (krjásăk, “shout, cry”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to wane, to wilt, to wither (of person, plant)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krěja /*kraja, cognate with Serbo-Croatian кре́ја (“jay, shriek”). Probably of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Russian кра́чка (kráčka, “tern”).

parole.significato: skew, slanting, crooked, bent, twisted, curved
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *krivъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kréiwas. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian крив/kriv, Slovene kriv, Russian криво́й (krivój), Slovak krivý, Polish krzywy; as well as with Latin curvus.

parole.significato: injustice, wrong, unfairness, injury (an unjust act, wrong, or unfair treatment done to someone)
wing, pinion (an appendage of an animal's (bird, bat, insect) body that enables it to fly)
meekness, gentleness, mildness, quietness (the quality of being gentle, calm, mild, or submissive in character or behav…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krotostь. By surface analysis, кро́тък (krótăk) + -ост (-ost)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krotъkъ. Formed with the adjectival suffix -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to tailor (garment, leather), to measure and cut (paper, metal sheet)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krǫtъ, with some of the meanings influenced by Russian круто́й (krutój, “drastic”).

parole.significato: to destroy, to shatter, to smash
cask, vat for storing winter supplies (such as sauerkraut, pickles, etc.)
parole.testo: Cognate with dialectal Serbo-Croatian кр̏бао (“measure for wine”), кр̀буља (“basket”). Further derived from Proto-Slavic *kъrbъ, *kъrba + -ла (-la).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krъvьnъ. By surface analysis, кръв (krăv, “blood”) + -ен (-en, adjectival suffix).

parole.significato: cycle, circulation, round, recurrence (a repeated circular or cyclical process in which things return, recur, or pass t…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krǫgovortъ. By surface analysis, кръг (krăg) + -о- (-o-) + вра́т (vrát)

parole.significato: to circle, to hover (of birds, insects, aircraft)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kъrzъ, *(s)krozě. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian кро̏з, Ukrainian крізь (krizʹ), Czech krůz, Slovak kroz. Old Church Slavonic скрозѣ (skrozě) probably results from a confluence of кръз (krăz) with synonymous скво́зе (skvóze).

parole.significato: layer of grime that has formed on the fur of mammals or on the skin of people

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *kъrnъ, technically a past passive participle of a root-verb probably from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut”). Attested in Old Church Slavonic крънъ (krŭnŭ, “marked, having a scar”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kukati. By surface analysis, ку-ку (ku-ku) + -кам (-kam).

parole.significato: kuker (person dressed in a carnival costume, who chases evil spirits in specific days of the year)
parole.testo: Technically reflecting Proto-Slavic *kukyrъ, possibly derived from Proto-Slavic *kukъ, *kuka (“feisty spirit”) + -ер (-er). Alternative theories propose borrowed origin from a term, akin to Bulgarian кукла (kukla, “toy, puppet”) (Greek loanword) or Bulgarian гу́гла (gúgla, “hood”) (Latin loanword),
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kukъla, from the root of Russian ку́ча (kúča, “heap”) + -ла (-la).
From Proto-Slavic *kukavica, *kukačьka, of onomatopoeic origin from the call ку-ку (ku-ku, “coo-coo”). Compare Latin cucūlus (“cuckoo”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopa. Doublet of копа́ (kopá).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kupiti (“to purchase”), of Gothic origin.

parole.significato: to aggregate, to amass, to stack up
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kupiti (“to pile”). Synchronically, the causative-iterative of куп (kup, “pile, heap”). In the modern language, perceived as an imperfective variant of Etymology 1.
From Proto-Slavic *kurъ (“rooster”), probably of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Bulgarian пу́тка (pútka, “duck; female genitalia”) for similar semantic shift.

parole.significato: wild hen (non-domestic bird of genus Gallus or more generally of order Galliformes)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kurъka; equivalent to кур (kur, “rooster”) (obsolescent) + -ка (-ka). Cognate with Macedonian ќурка (ḱurka, “turkey”), Serbo-Croatian ħу̏рка (“turkey”). Further loaned into Romanian curcă (“turkey hen”).

parole.significato: mortar (wooden or stony receptacle in which ingredients are ground)
parole.testo: Unclear. Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary lists as possible origins: * Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kutьlъ, whence also dial. Serbo-Croatian ку̏тао (“spade”), from the root of Proto-Slavic *kuti (“to hew”); * Possibly borrowed from a Vulgar Latin reflex of Latin cotyla (“beaker”) or Ancient Greek κ

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kutrъ, cognate with Macedonian кутре (kutre, “puppy”), of unclear further origin. Proposed hypotheses include: * Of onomatopoeic origin, related to the call кут-кут (kut-kut) (for calling up canines or birds), initially referring specifically to puppies or cubs and later

parole.significato: to heed, to coddle, to take care (of a child, an animal)
parole.testo: Reflects Proto-Slavic *kutiti (possibly *kǫtiti), with original meaning unclear. Proposed etymologies: * Of grammatical origin: An o-vocalism of outdated Bulgarian чу́тя (čútja, “to perceive, to comprehend”), from a t-extension of Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to perceive”). Akin to Bulgarian чу́
From Proto-Slavic *kucъ. Unrelated to Bulgarian кутсу́з (kutsúz, “unlucky, hapless”) (of Turkish origin).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kucati. By surface analysis, куц (kuc) + -ам (-am), of expressive origin.
From Proto-Slavic *kǫčiti, *kučiti. Cognate with Polish dokuczyć pf (“to tease, to annoy, to trouble”) and possibly Russian кучиться (kučitʹsja, “to clump, to stack”).

Not clear. Per BER, most plausibly via semantic shift from Proto-Slavic *kǫblo (“lair, nest”) + -я (-ja). Akin to Old Polish kęblać (“to nourish, to feed”), kęblić (“to rise, to tend”), dialectal Russian ку́блиться (kúblitʹsja, “to nest”).

parole.significato: sliver, bundle of unspun threads (prepared for spinning)
curl, ringlet, lock (of hair or fur)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kǫdravъ, *kǫdřavъ, cognate with Macedonian кадрав (kadrav), Russian ку́дрявый (kúdrjavyj). Morphologically equivalent to къ́дря (kắdrja, “to curl hair”) + -ав (-av).

parole.significato: distaff, spinning rock (particularly: the conical upper part where one attaches the fibres)

parole.testo: Conflation of Proto-Slavic *kǫkolъ and *kǫkylь. Superseded in the modern language by its derivative къ́клица (kắklica) (originally referring to the seeds of the plant).

parole.significato: upper muscular portion of the leg
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъlka (“bony stump”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kulˀk-. Per Derksen, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁- (“to turn”). Cognates include Macedonian колк (kolk, “hip”), Russian колк (kolk, “bony stump”), Serbo-Croatian kuk (“thigh, hip”) and Lithuanian kulkšnis (“an
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъlnъ, a n-derivative from lost **kъlti, cognate with Lithuanian kùlti (“to prod, to knock”), Latvian kul̃t (“to thresh”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krъvavъ. By surface analysis, кръв (krăv) + -ав (-av).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъrža, deverbal from *kъrgati (whence Slovene kŕgati (“to coagulate”)).

parole.significato: to gulp, to guzzle, to swig (to drink noisily, greedily, or in large gulps)
parole.testo: Blend of Etymology 1 with Proto-Slavic *kъrkati (“to contort”).

parole.significato: to cradle, to be swinging, to be dandling
parole.testo: Proto-Slavic *kъrľь (“something hanging”) + -уя (-uja) (formally equivalent to an earlier *kъrľevati).

parole.significato: to suckle, to breastfeed, to nurse
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъrmiti (“to nourish”). By surface analysis, кърма (kărma, “breast milk”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: mole (burrowing mammal of the family Talpidae)
to break, to crack, to peck (with a tool)
to break off, to snap, to tear off (branches, twigs, vines)
late (near the end of a period of time, e.g. a day, season, or historical period)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъsьnъ, of uncertain origin. Possibly from an earlier *kъtsьnъ with meaning spoiled, passed its deadline, related to Bulgarian ки́сна (kísna, “to soak, to ferment”). According to Al. T. Balan, from къ (k, “towards”) + сън (săn, “dream, sleep”). See also къ́сно (kắsno).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kǫtъ. Further origin is either from the root of Proto-Slavic *kǫpъ (“thicket, bush; kink”) or less likely related to къ́там (kắtam, “to conceal”), къ́тна (kắtna, “to nudge”) (both of unclear origin).

parole.significato: to hide, to conceal, to keep (something) hidden
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kǫtati. Possibly akin to English hide, hut.
From Proto-Slavic *kǫšьjь (or from *kǫsьjь, *kǫsějь with expressive palatalization of *-s- > *-š-). Equivalent to къс (kăs, “piece, bite”) + -ей (-ej).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *oldi (ī-stem), reanalyzed as a ja-stem in -ия (-ija). Doublet of лодка (lodka) (East Slavic borrowing).

parole.significato: glade, dell (place within a forest where the trees have been cut down)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lazъ (“plowed land”), of uncertain origin. Possibly: * Identical to Etymology 1, derived via semantic shift “inlet (into a forest)” → “glade”; * From the root of Russian лозг (lozg, “crack”), ложжи́ть (ložžítʹ, “to delve”); * Akin to Latvian lēzs (“even, flat”), lēzа (“c

Uncertain: * Mladenov: Modified deverbal of ле́я (léja, “to pour”) + -ка (-ka), presumably from an earlier *ляйка. * Lj. Kurkina: Deverbal of Proto-Slavic *lajati (“to lie in ambush”) + -ка (-ka). Doublets have been confused (by folk etymology) for a compound of лай (laj, “barking”) + куче (kuče, “d
From Proto-Slavic *olkomъ; equivalent to алча (alča, “to hunger for”) + -ом (-om).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *olkъtь. By surface analysis, (obsolescent) лак (lak) + -ът (-ăt).

parole.significato: sleet, slush (mixture of rain, snow, and/or hail)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *xlapa with colloquial elision of initial #x-, cognate with Polish chlapa. Perhaps related to Lithuanian šlãpias (“wet”), šlãpė (“damp place or land”).

parole.significato: to gulp, to gobble, to swallow

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lasica. Originally, the standard word for weasel. Nowadays, superseded by its epithets невесту́лка (nevestúlka), бу́лчица (búlčica) or кадъ́нка (kadắnka) (literally: “little bride, maid”), probably due to tabu avoidance.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *laskavъ. Equivalent to ла́ска (láska, “caress”) + -ав (-av).

parole.significato: to flatter, to adulate, to jolly
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *laskati. By surface analysis, ласка (laska, “caress”) + -а́я (-ája).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lěvakъ. By surface analysis, ляв (ljav, “left”) + -ак (-ak).

parole.significato: to assume a horizontal position, to lie, to lie down
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *leťi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *légtei, from Proto-Indo-European *légʰeti, from *legʰ-.

parole.significato: final stage of sickness just before healing
parole.testo: From an earlier льгоба (lĭgoba, “ease”), a derivative from Proto-Slavic *lьgъ (“mild, light”) + -оба (-oba). Akin to Russian облегче́ние (oblexčénije, “relief”), Slovene ləgóta (“ease”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lędo. Cognate with English land.

Fossilized plurale tantum of Proto-Slavic *lędvьje (attested as Old Church Slavonic лѧдвиѩ pl (lędviję, “loins”)), probably spread from western dialects. Compare Serbo-Croatian ле́ђа pl (“back”). Semantic shift analogous to Bulgarian коля́но (koljáno, “generation, lineage”) (literally: knee).
From Proto-Slavic *lędina; equivalent to ле́да (léda, “untilled land”) (dialectal) + -ина (-ina).
From Proto-Slavic *lьgъkъ, formed from a lost *lьgъ (“mild”) + -ък (-ăk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lěkařь. By surface analysis, лек (lek) + -ар (-ar).

parole.significato: to cherish, to harbor, to nurture (a dream, feeling, etc. in one's soul)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lemezь /*lemežь /*lemešь. Cognate with Lithuanian lemežis (“cleft”).

parole.significato: linen (plant of family Linaceae, most commonly of genus Linum)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lěnь (i-stem), substantivized from an earlier adjective лѣнъ (lěnŭ, “lazy”) (attested in Old Church Slavonic).
From Proto-Slavic *lěnivъ (“lazy, sluggish”). Formed as лен (len, “laziness”) + -ив (-iv).

parole.significato: laziness, idleness, sloth, indolence (the quality or state of being lazy, inactive, or unwilling to work or make effort)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lěnostь. By surface analysis, лен (len) + -ост (-ost).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lepetъ. Parallel to Old Church Slavonic лопотивъ (lopotivŭ, “stuttering”) (with o-grade). A similar formation is found in Sanskrit लप् (lap, “to chatter”).
From Proto-Slavic *lěpidlo; equivalent to лепя (lepja, “to glue”) + -ило (-ilo).
Probably from Proto-Slavic *lěpyrь; equivalent to лепя́ (lepjá, “to stick up”) + -ир (-ir). Compare also Serbo-Croatian ле̏птӣр (“butterfly”) (usually thought to be of Greek origin).

parole.significato: to glue, to paste, to stick

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *lěsišče, an augmentative form of лес (les, “forest”) + -ище (-ište).

parole.significato: hazel (shrub or tree of genus Corylus)
bed for plants, garden plot (а raised shaped area of soil (such as a quadrangle, ellipse, etc.), convenient for plantin…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lě̄xà, whence also Old Church Slavonic лѣха (lěxa).
From Proto-Slavic *lěčimъ. Morphologically equivalent to лек (lek, “remedy”) + -им (-im).

parole.significato: lentil plant (legume plant of genus Lens, most often of species Lens culinaris)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lęťa, a wanderwort cognate with Latin lēns.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *libavъ ~ *liběvъ, whence also Old Church Slavonic либавъ (libavŭ), либѣвъ (liběvŭ). Cognate (via another suffix) with Russian либи́вый (libívyj, “thin”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *livъ. Synchronically, a deverbal of ли́я (líja, “to pour”).
From Proto-Slavic *ligavъ. Morphologically equivalent to ли́га (líga, “slobber, drool”) + -ав (-av).

parole.significato: to look around, to watch out for threats in various directs
to lick (to stroke with the tongue)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *likъ (“face”), of disputed origin. Possibly deverbal of ли́я (líja, “to pour, to cast”) with original meaning “contour, layout”.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *likъ (“play”), probably of Germanic origin, although the exact source is unknown (compare Gothic 𐌻𐌰𐌹𐌺𐌰𐌽 (laikan, “to jump around”)).
From Proto-Slavic *lilъ (“thin membrane”), cognate with Serbo-Croatian лѝла (“smooth tree bark”) (dialectal).

parole.significato: to languish, to wilt, to fade away
lime tree, linden tree (tree of genus Tilia)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *lipъkъ (“flexible”). Related to Bulgarian леп (lep, “sticky, beautiful”). Formed with the suffix -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: bald, bare-headed (of a person: having partly or wholly lost the hair on the head)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lisica, parsable as (poetic) ли́са (lísa) + -ица (-ica).
From Proto-Slavic *listьje (“leafage”), originally meaning cluster of leaves. Morphologically, equivalent to лист (list, “leaf”) + -е (-e).

parole.significato: leaf fall (the falling of leaves from trees and plants, especially in autumn)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *listopadъ. By surface analysis, лист (list) + -о- (-o-) + па́д (pád)

parole.significato: to roam, to meander, to rove
interest (the price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calcul…
hypocrite, dissembler, pretender (a person who outwardly shows virtues, beliefs, feelings, or intentions that they do n…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *licemĕrъ. By surface analysis, лице (lice) + ме́ря (mérja)

parole.significato: to discern, to distinguish, to recognize

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *ličьba. Morphologically equivalent to лича́ (ličá, “to seem, to indicate”) + -ба (-ba). Compare Macedonian лиџба (lidžba, “beauty”).

parole.significato: to deprive, to strip, to bereave (to take away from someone something that they have, need, or are entitled to)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *lišьjь (a doublet of Proto-Slavic *lišajь whence dialectal ли́шай (líšaj)). Equivalent to лих (lih, “contentious”) + -ей (-ej).

parole.significato: orach, saltbush (garden plant of genus Atriplex)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *loboda /*olboda, of unclear origin. Either borrowed from an uncertain source or, if native, equivalent to *lobъ (“bottom, bed”) or *olb- (“albus”) + -ода (-oda).

parole.significato: bed, couch, bedstead, resting place (a place prepared for lying, sleeping, or resting)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lomъ. Different senses probably diachronically heterogenous.

parole.significato: to break, to smash, to shatter (to make something solid into pieces with a blow)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lono, of unclear origin. Perhaps from (obsolete) лог (log, “post, seat”) + -сно (-sno) (in Slavic *-g-sno > *-xno > *-no), related to Proto-Slavic *ložesno (“womb”).
From Proto-Slavic *lopata. Morphologically formed from лоп- (lop-, “sheet, spade”) + -ата (-ata).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lopěnъ, equivalent to лоп (lop) (dialectal) + -ян (-jan).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lopurъ. By surface analysis, лоп (lop, “leaf, foliage”) (dialectal) + -ур (-ur).

parole.significato: to lap (to consume liquid using one's tongue)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lugъ m, *luga f, probably of Germanic origin (see Proto-Germanic *laugō (“lye”)). Mladenov tentatively considers a native origin (at least for some of the meanings), comparing it with native Bulgarian слуз (sluz) (with s-mobile), dial. лу́за (lúza, “mucus”) and possibly

parole.significato: to smack, to tug something off
parole.testo: Deverbal factitive from Proto-Slavic *luzga (“peel”), possibly related to Etymology 1. Attested in Old Church Slavonic лꙋзгати (luzgati).

parole.significato: onion (monocotyledonous flowering plant of genus Allium)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *lǫkavъ, whence also Old Church Slavonic лѫкавъ (lǫkavŭ), Slovene lokav, Russian лука́вый (lukávyj).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lǫkavьstvo. By surface analysis, лука́в (lukáv) + -ство (-stvo).

parole.significato: grove, wood, hurst (place overgrown with vegetation)
to tell an untruth, lie, tell stories, speak with a forked tongue
to polish, to burnish, to furbish
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lъskati (equivalent to *lъk- + *-skati), akin to English light. By the time of first Slavic writing, the root has been reanalyzed into *lьsk- (cf. Old Church Slavonic льщати (lĭštati)), which BER explains as an influence from synonymous *blьskati (“to flash”).

parole.significato: flattery, adulation, blandishment (insincere or flattering speech used to please, attract, or gain advantage)
to whiff, to puff, to blow softly (of wind)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lǫťa, of Celtic origin. Cognate with Latin lancea, possibly Ancient Greek λόγχη (lónkhē, “spearhead”).

parole.significato: love, devotion, affection (selfless attachment usually towards one's homeland, family, or an idea)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ľuby. An alternative form of любъ́в (ljubắv), but with a vocalised strong yer. Attested in a Tarnovo recension Middle Bulgarian manuscript from the early 1400s, so either one of the few cases of strong yer vocalisation in Eastern Bulgarian or influenced by Western Bulgar

parole.significato: to love, to be fond of
to rock, to swing, to dandle
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ľulěti, *ľuľati, of imitative origin.

parole.significato: to husk, to scale, to hull
parole.testo: * Meaning “to husk”: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *luskati (“to husk”). * Meaning “to slam”: Expressive extension of the primary meaning, possibly partially onomatopoeic. The palatal pronunciation of initial #лʲ- is expressive.

parole.significato: to husk, to scale, to hull (to remove husks, scales, hulls)
parole.testo: Causative-iterative from nowadays obsolete/dialectal лю́ска (ljúska, “scale, husk”) + -я (-ja) (< Proto-Slavic *ľuska). Expressive semantics (listed by some dictionary as a separate etymon) is from related interjection люс (ljus, “whoosh”).

parole.significato: to creep, to crawl, to proceed slowly

parole.testo: Fossilized perfective participle of Proto-Slavic *liti (“to flow, to shed”).

parole.significato: to spread butter, to grease, to anoint once
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *maznǫti, synchronically a ne-inchoative of *mazati (“to anoint, to spread”).

parole.significato: poppy (flower of the family Papaveraceae, primarily of the genus Papaver)
to dip, to soak, to souse
to lose strength, to grow faint, to wither
parole.testo: Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary tentatively presumes the same origin as Etymology 1. Per Duridanov, more likely a reanalysis of Proto-Slavic *mъdьlěti (“to get tardy”).
From Proto-Slavic *malъkъ, a doublet of Proto-Slavic *malъ. Morphologically analysable as from dialectal мал (mal, “small”) + -ък (-ăk).
A nursery word, inherited from Proto-Slavic *mama.

parole.significato: to deceive, to cheat, to scam, to defraud
to concern, to care (usually with за (za), по (po), от (ot))
oil, oily, oil-based (relating to oil or containing oil)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *maslěnъ. By surface analysis, ма́сло (máslo) + -ен (-en)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mastidlo, synchronically parsable as мастя́ (mastjá, “to paint”) + -ило (-ilo) (instrumental suffix).

parole.significato: motherhood, maternity (the state, condition, or role of being a mother)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *materinьstvo. By surface analysis, ма́терен (máteren) + -ство (-stvo).

parole.significato: adult ram or billygoat (usually used for breeding)
parole.testo: Substantivized agent noun from the adjective Proto-Slavic *matorъ (“mature”).
Deverbal from (obsolete) ма́я (mája, “to sway”) (reflexive ма́я се (mája se, “to hesitate”) is still standard). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *maxъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *maxati. By surface analysis, мах (mah, “swish”) + -ам (-am).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *macati. Possibly an expressive variant of dialectal ма́ча (máča)/ма́кам (mákam, “to dip, to plunge; to souse (food)”) or of ма́жа (máža, “to smear”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mačьka, probably of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: to squash, to crush, to maul (to mutilate by pressing and squeezing)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mačьkati. Morphologically, from a long grade of (obsolete) ме́ча (méča, “to thrust, to press”) + -кам (-kam).
Per the Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary, derived from a putative stem *maťer- of Proto-Slavic *mati. Otherwise, a variant of Proto-Slavic *materъka - again a derivation from a case form of *mati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *majati. Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary distinguish the meaning “to delay, to dally” (under мая¹) from “to mesmerise, to wonder” (under мая²).
Conflation of Proto-Slavic *meděnъ and *medьnъ. Morphologically, from мед (med, “honey”) + -ен (-en).
From мед (med, “honey”) + -еница (-enica). Formally reflects an earlier Proto-Slavic *meděnica (“honey product”).
From мед (med, “honey”) + -енка (-enka). Formally reflects an earlier Proto-Slavic *meděnъka (“honey product”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *medovina, morphologically equivalent to мед (med, “honey”) + -овина (-ovina).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mękъkъ. By surface analysis, ме́ча (méča, “to knead, to press”) + -ък (-ăk) (the base verb has been lost, but secondary derivatives are still attested in dialects).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mękyšь. By surface analysis, ме́чам (méčam, “to knead”) (dialectal) + -иш (-iš).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *melivo. By surface analysis, ме́ля (mélja, “to grind, to mill”) + -иво (-ivo)

parole.significato: scutcher (old-fashioned tool for scutching linen, hemp, flax, or other fibers)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *melьnica. By surface analysis, ме́ля (mélja, “to grind, to mill”) + -ница (-nica).
From Proto-Slavic *měrъ (“gauge”), indirectly attested in derivatives.
From Proto-Slavic *měračь; equivalent to ме́ря (mérja, “to measure”), dialectal ме́рям (mérjam, “to estimate, to narrow down, to aim”) + -ач (-ač).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měrьnъ; equivalent to мя́ра (mjára, “measure”) + -ен (-en).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měrenъ. Synchronically, a substantivized past passive participle of меря (merja, “to measure”) + -ен (-en).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měridlo. By surface analysis, меря (merja, “to measure”) + -ило (-ilo).

parole.significato: hindsight, aimer (part of a projectile weapon used for aiming at a target)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *měrьnikъ. Morphologically, equivalent to ме́ря (mérja, “to measure”) + -ник (-nik).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měriti. Morphologically, a causative-iterative of мя́ра (mjára, “measure, extend”).

parole.significato: to move, to shift, to transfer to a new place
parole.testo: Causative-iterative of място (mjasto, “place”), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *městiti.

parole.significato: mint (herb of genus Mentha, within the Lamiaceae family)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *męty (v-stem), ultimately of substrate origin. Superseded by its doublet ме́нта (ménta) (Latin borrowing).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mętežь. By surface analysis, Proto-Slavic *męti (“to trample”) + -еж (-ež).
From Proto-Slavic *motyľь (“insect, parasite”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian мѐтӣљ (“fluke”), Slovene metìlj, metùlj (“butterfly”), dialectal Russian меты́ль (metýlʹ, “moth, mayfly”).
From Proto-Slavic *metъla, morphologically from мета́ (metá, “to sweep”) + -ла (-la).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měxyrь. By surface analysis, мях (mjah, “bellows”) + -ур (-ur).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mečь, of unclear origin. In view of the doublet form *mьčь (whence e.g. Serbo-Croatian ма̏ч), borrowing from a foreign language is the most prevalent theory.

parole.significato: to knead, to press, to apply force/thrust into something

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьčьta, parsable as Proto-Slavic *mikati + -та (-ta).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měšati. By surface analysis, ме́ся (mésja) + -ям (-jam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *migъ (“blink”) via semantic shift “blink, wink” → “short moment of time”.

parole.significato: to blink (to close and open the eyes quickly)
to blink (to close and open the eyes quickly once)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mězinъ (“younger, smaller”) + -ец (-ec), possibly blended with an agent noun of *midzati / *mizgati (“to caress, to smooch”). The unexpected root -и- may be also a result of narrowing of unstressed open vowels, which is regular within Eastern dialects (but not in the West).

parole.significato: to fondle, to caress, to stroke lovingly
to hold dear, to be fond of (usually with за (za))

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mydlo, synchronically parsable as мия (mija, “to wash”) + -ло (-lo) (instrumental suffix). Attested among Lovech Pomaks.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *milostь. By surface analysis, мил (mil, “gentle”) + -ост (-ost).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *milostivъ. By surface analysis, милост (milost) + -ив (-iv)

parole.significato: merciful, compassionate, charitable, kind-hearted (showing pity, compassion, and readiness to help those who suffer)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *milosьrdьnъ. By surface analysis, ми́л (míl) + -о- (-o-) + съ́рце (sắrce) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to pass by, to elapse (of time)
to pass by, to elapse (of time)
peace (a state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mirьba. Morphologically equivalent to мир (mir, “piece”) + -ба (-ba).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mirьnъ. By surface analysis, мир (mir) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to pacify, to appease, to reconcile (hostile parties)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *miriti. Synchronically, a causative-iterative of мир (mir, “peace”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mitъ, formally a t-participle of unattested *miti (“to pass, to proceed”) (see factitive extension *mijati).

parole.significato: customs duty, duty, tariff (a tax or charge imposed by the state on goods imported into or exported from a country)
to shove, to propel, to drag, to thrust

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *myšьjь. By surface analysis, миш(ка) (miš(ka)) + -и (-i).

parole.significato: to wash (to clean something with water or another liquid)
youth (the period of life when a person is young)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *moldostь. By surface analysis, млад (mlad) + -ост (-ost).
From Proto-Slavic *molkъ or *mlakъ, limited to South Slavic.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *molka, cognate with Serbo-Croatian мла̏ка (“puddle”), Old East Slavic молокита (molokita, “marsh”). Probably further related to Czech mlkvý (“raw”). According to some scholars, possibly akin to Proto-Slavic *melko (“milk”) (whence native мля́ко (mljáko)).

parole.significato: to beat, to thwack, to strike something with a mallet (or another tool)

parole.testo: Either a conflation of dialectal млези́во (mlezívo, “colostrum”) and мъзга́ (măzgá, “sap”), or perhaps from an earlier Proto-Slavic *melzga (no direct cognates in other Slavic languages).

parole.significato: latex, plant's sap (milk-like substance released by some plants)
milky, milk, dairy (products derived from or containing milk)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *melčьnъ. By surface analysis, мля́ко (mljáko) + -ен (-en).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mlinъ (from 0-grade of ме́ля (mélja, “to mince”) + -ин (-in)).

parole.significato: to fall silent, to stop speaking/talking, to shut up

parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Slavic *mьněti (“to think, believe”). By surface analysis, мня (mnja) + -ение (-enie).
From Proto-Slavic *mьnimъ, the past active participle of мня (mnja, “to mind”) (dialectal) + -им (-im).

Derived from Proto-Slavic *mъnogъ, originally a fully-fletched adjective, eventually reanalysed as an indeclinable adverb. Fossilized plural forms мно́зи m (mnózi) and мно́га n (mnóga) (for example, in the poetic expression мно́гая ле́та (mnógaja léta, “many years”)) are attested in dialects and lit

parole.significato: to multiply (to increase a number, quantity, or amount many times)
to opine, to reckon, to deem (to have an opinion)

parole.testo: Simplified from an earlier мозг (mozg), with final -г devoiced (as usual for word-final voiced stops) and later interpreted as the diminutive suffix -ък (-ăk). Ultimately, inherited from Proto-Slavic *mozgъ.

parole.significato: wet, humid, moisty (having excess of moisture)
filled up cavity, pocket, pothole (hole under a surface, usually obscured by a rock, vegetation, or filled with some ma…
parole.testo: BER tentatively suggests origin from Proto-Slavic *molъ, derived via o-grade ablaut from the root of ме́ля (mélja, “to grind”). Compare Lithuanian malti (“to grind”), Latvian malt (“to grind”) (with o-grade).
From Proto-Slavic *modlьba. Morphologically equivalent to мо́ля (mólja, “to beg, to pray”) + -ба (-ba).
Derived from Proto-Slavic *modla, reshaped to resemble ja-stems во́ля (vólja, “will”), dial. до́ля (dólja, “lot, fate”).

parole.significato: carrot (a vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, family Apiaceae…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mъrky. Originally a feminine (referring to the plant as a whole), later reanalyzed as a masculine (referring specifically to the root).

parole.significato: to drain one's energy, vitality, strength
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *moriti, causative-iterative of мор (mor, “exhaustion, withering”).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *motyka.
