parole.significato: to wet, to moisten, to damp
pod, follicle (seed case of beans, peas, okra, or other similar plants)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mošьna (“sack”), with undergone semantic shift. Still attested with its original meaning in Old Church Slavonic мошьна (mošĭna).

parole.significato: ant (eusocial insect of family Formicidae, most often of genera Formica or Myrmica)
dark, gloomy, dim (without enough light; dark or poorly lit)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *morčьnъ. By surface analysis, мрак (mrak) + -ен (-en).

According to Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary, inherited from Proto-Slavic *merzgavъ, akin to 0-grade verb мръ́ждя (mrắždja, “to glimmer”). Has been also compared with Proto-Slavic *brězgъ (“downbreak”), on the assumption of irregular alternation *br- ↔ *mr-. Gerov spells the lemma with nasal -ѧ-,

Blend of Proto-Slavic *nerstiti (“to spawn”) and *mьrskati (“to besmirch, to soil; fig. to fertilize”) (whence dialectal/obsolete Bulgarian мръ́скам (mrắskam)). Similar portmanteau is observed throughout South Slavic languages, e.g. Macedonian се мрести (se mresti), Serbo-Croatian мрије́стити се, he

parole.significato: to kill, to decimate, to take one's vitality or consciousness (of illness or another ailment)
to wrinkle one's face, to pull in one's eyebrows, to frown, to make a wry face
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrzgati, *mьržďiti, an expressive variant of *mьrskati, *mьrščiti (whence the more common мръщя се (mrăštja se)).

parole.significato: to wrinkle, to knit, to furrow (one's face, forehead, eyebrows, etc. in an expression of displeasure)
to scowl, to frown, to make a wry face

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mudьnъ. Morphologically parsable as (dialectal) му́дя се (múdja se, “to languish, to get late”) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to pass or proceed (though something) slowly, laggardly

parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Slavic *muľь (“dampness, silt”) (whence Serbo-Croatian му̑љ (“mud”)) + -авя (-avja)

parole.significato: mule (offspring of a male donkey and a female horse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mulę, of substrate origin. Compare Latin mūlus, Ancient Greek μύκλος (múklos).
Unclear; either of substrate origin or a substantivized form of Proto-Slavic *murъ (“dusky, muddy”), whence Bulgarian мура́ва (muráva, “meadow”).

parole.significato: swarthy, dusky, murky (of hue or saturation)
fly (insect of genus Musca or more generally of family Muscidae)
to moo, to bellow (of ungulates: cows, deer)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mučati (ě/i-conjugation), of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: to take a nap, to drowse, to slumber
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьgnǫti (“to blink”), with shift of meaning “to blink/shut one's eyes” → “to go into slumber”.

parole.significato: wisdom, sagacity, sageness, prudence, common sense, good sense
wise, sage, sagacious, reasonable, sensible, sound, commonsense, judicious, prudent, discreet
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mǫdrъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mandrás, from Proto-Indo-European *men(s)dʰh₁-.

From Proto-Slavic *mъďa (“weakening, abatement”); equivalent to мъждя (măždja, “to fade away”) + -а (-a). Cognate with dialectal Russian мжа (mža, “day dream”), Czech mze pl (“tuberculose”) and akin to Russian ме́дленный (médlennyj, “slow”), Serbo-Croatian ма̏дал (“unclear, blur”), Slovene medel (“w
From an earlier мъжски (măžski), from Proto-Slavic *mǫžьskъ. Equivalent to мъж (măž, “man”) + -ски (-ski).
Blend of Proto-Slavic *mъzga (“mucus, silt”) (also borrowed into Romanian mâzgă (“slime”)) and *mězga (“sap”) (the later reflected by doublet Bulgarian мязга (mjazga)).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьzda. Superseded by Russian borrowing награ́да (nagráda).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫka (abstract noun), originally meaning “pressure, stress”.

parole.significato: to drag, to haul, to lug
to utter, to murmur, to say quietly
to milk (to draw off milk from a dairy animal)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьlziti, a causative-iterative variant of *melsti (whence Old Church Slavonic млѣсти (mlěsti)).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mъldni (ī-stem), eventually reanalyzed as a ьja-stem (as if ending in -ия (-ija)).

parole.significato: to be silent, to keep silence, to remain mum, to keep still (not to utter a sound)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *monisto, with darkening of unstressed -o- between nasals.
From Proto-Slavic *mьnь + -ичък (-ičăk), the old comparative stem of малък (malăk, “small”).

parole.significato: to move, to shift (position, place of something)
to stagnate, to get depleted, to lose strength or significance
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrzěti (ě/i-conjugation), *mьrziti (i-conjugation). Some dictionaries make distinction between the senses “to loathe” and “to idle”, but etymologically they stem from the same origin.

parole.significato: to oestruate, to rut, to go into heat (of animals, usually livestock)
parole.testo: Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary favours a grammatical origin from Proto-Slavic *mьrkati (“to smudge, to daub”) (implied also by Vasmer in relation to probable cognate Russian мереча (mereča, “sludge”)). Other hypotheses view it as a figurative sense of onomatopoeic мъ́ркам (mắrkam, “to purr”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrlъ (“depleted, perished”). Attested in substantivized form and in secondary derivatives.

parole.significato: to stroke, to prod, to besmirch
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrliti (“to besmirch, to soil”), distantly akin to English smear. Some dictionaries distinguish the meaning “to besmirch” from “to fertilize”.
From Proto-Slavic *mьrľavъ. Morphologically equivalent to мърла (mărla, “slattern”) (dialectal) + -яв (-jav).

parole.significato: to murmur or mutter (usually) to oneself out of annoyance, displeasure, anger, etc.; to grumble
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mъrmoriti, whence also Serbo-Croatian мрморити, of onomatopoeic origin. For similar onomatopoeiae, compare English murmur, Albanian mërmërit, Latin murmurō, Ancient Greek μορμύρω (mormúrō).

parole.significato: to make dirty, to besmirch, to stain

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrxa (“decay”). The plant bears its name because of its repulsive odour.

parole.significato: to get / grow dark, dim, dusky
parole.testo: Causative-iterative of dialectal мърк (mărk, “dark, dim”), inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrčiti.
ja-stem variant of Proto-Slavic *mьrxa (“decay”). Attested as мьръша (mĭrŭša), мръша (mrŭša) in Church Slavonic.

parole.significato: mule (hybrid between a male donkey and a female horse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mъskъ, probably of Paleo-Balkan descent, akin to Albanian mushk (“mule”), Aromanian mușcă (“mule”), Latin mūlus (“mule”) (<*muslos), Ancient Greek μυχλός (mukhlós, “he-ass”). Further origin is unclear. Meyer hypothesizes a possible relation to the ethnonym of the ancient people My

parole.significato: [with на (na)] to avenge, to take revenge (to pay back for an evil deed)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *mǫtьnъ. Morphologically formed as мъ́тя (mắtja, “to stir, to puddle”) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: flour bin, crate (box in which flour is collected during milling)
parole.testo: Equivalent to Proto-Slavic *mǫka (product noun) + -ник (-nik). The base noun is attested within older literature as obs. мука́ (muká), which is a Russian borrowing.

parole.significato: measurement standard, norm (an object or a reference against which a measurement is done)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měra, a deverbal noun of ме́ря (mérja, “to measure”).

parole.significato: to throw, to cast, to toss
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mětati, derived via vṛddhi from *metati (“to throw”).

parole.significato: on, onto, upon (forming words and verbs denoting position, placement, or movement onto a surface or toward a place)
to drive in (to force something into something else by striking, pressing, or pushing)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naborъ (equivalent to *na- + *borъ (“assembly”)). Meaning “cohort” is borrowed from Russian набо́р (nabór), from the same proto-Slavic word.

parole.significato: to wrick, to twist, to sprain
parole.testo: From на- (na-) + *вехна (*vehna, “to get twisted”) (an inchoative of Proto-Slavic *věxati, whence Slovene véhati (“to waver”)). Not to be confused with attested ве́хна (véhna, “to fade, to wilt”), which descends from unrelated *vędnǫti.

parole.significato: evening (period of the day immediately before the eve)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *navečerьje; equivalent to на- (na-) + ве́чер (véčer, “eve”) + -ие (-ie).
Plural form of Proto-Slavic *navь. Probably akin to *nyti (“to ache, to wither”).
Deverbal of нави́квам (navíkvam, “to get used to”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *navykъ.

parole.significato: to get used (to become used to something or begin doing something habitually)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *navolkъ, formed as на- (na-) + влак (vlak, “drag, train”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *na vъnъ. By surface analysis, univerbation of на (na) + вън (văn).

parole.significato: overwatching, supervision (monitoring from a superior position)
parole.testo: By surface analysis, над- (nad-) + (obsolescent) зор (zor, “vision, view”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *nadъzorъ.

parole.significato: to overtake, to outstrip, to get ahead of someone in a race or contest
Forms the superlative of adjectives and adverbs.; most, -est

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nakazъ. In the modern language, superseded by the verbal noun нака́зание (nakázanie).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nakana; equivalent to на- (na-) + ка́я се (kája se, “to regret, to repent one’s sins”) + -на (-na).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naklonъ. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + клон (klon, “skewing”).
Deverbal of нало́жа pf (nalóža, “to set up”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *nalogъ.

parole.significato: full form of the first-person plural pronoun in the dative case, used as the indirect object of a verb; to us, for us,…
mound, heap of dirt, soil, materials (which have been swept off)
parole.testo: Deverbal of намета́ (nametá, “to sweep into a mound”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *nametъ.
Deverbal of намя́там (namjátam, “to toss on”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *namĕtъ.

parole.significato: accumulation of materials brought in one place
parole.testo: O-grade deverbal of нанеса́ (nanesá, “to carry on, to inflict”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *nanosъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napadъ. Synchronically, an action noun of напа́дам (napádam, “to go down”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napastь. Syncronically, a deverbal of напа́дам (napádam, “to assault”). By surface analysis, на- (na-) + паст (past, “chasm, rift”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napętъ, a fossilized t-participle of напъ́на (napắna, “to strain, to exert”).

parole.significato: to write something completely, to write down
place or occasion where one drinks
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napojь. By surface analysis, deverbal from напи́я (napíja, “to make s.o. drunk”)
O-grade deverbal of напъ́на (napắna, “to strain”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *naponъ. In the standard language, superseded by its 0-grade doublet на́пън (nápăn).
O-grade deverbal of напра́ (naprá, “to thrust on, to shove”). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *naporъ.

parole.significato: to press, to thrust, to propel
parole.testo: By surface analysis, на- (na-) + пра (pra). Diachronically, inherited from Proto-Slavic *naperti.

parole.significato: futile, unavailing (that which is in vain)

parole.significato: abrupt, sudden, unexpected, occurring at once
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naprasьnъ, of unclear origin. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic напрасьнъ (naprasĭnŭ, “quick, swift”), Serbo-Croatian на́прасан (“unabated”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narędъ. Doublet of наря́д (narjád) (Russian borrowing).

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nasilovati. By surface analysis, наси́ля (nasílja) + -вам (-vam).

parole.significato: to jump up, to spring up, to leap up (for several or many people or animals to jump, leap, or rise suddenly)

parole.significato: to tuck, to skewer, to impale

parole.testo: From an earlier *natьra, deverbal of Proto-Slavic *naterti (“to rub off”).

parole.significato: to be indignant, to resent, to be outraged

uncomfortable, unwieldy (difficult to wear or use)

parole.significato: nail (the thin, horny plate at the ends of fingers and toes on humans and some other animals)

parole.significato: inula, elecampane (Inula spp., especially Inula helenium)

parole.significato: support, prop, stay (an object, part, or structure on which something rests or by which it is held up)

From Proto-Slavic *otъpečatьkъ, from *pečatь. Analyzable as отпеча́там (otpečátam, “to print down”) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: prophet (a person believed to speak by divine inspiration or to reveal the will of God)

parole.significato: clearing, cutting, cut-through, cut line (a strip cut through forest, bushes, or dense vegetation)

parole.significato: space, expanse, spaciousness, room (amount of space), commodiousness
spacious, roomy, large, wide (having much space; broad, large, or not cramped)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *proxolda. By surface analysis, про- (pro-) + хлада (hlada).

parole.significato: to cool, to refresh (to make someone or something pleasantly cool)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *prъsnǫti / *pъrsnǫti, formed with the perfective suffix *-nǫti from *prъskati / *pъrskati (with regular loss of the consonant *k before the nasal *n.

parole.significato: ring (a round piece of metal worn around the finger)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьrsty (n-stem), equivalent to пръст (prăst, “finger”) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: raw flesh, meat, entrails without fat

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *puskati. Compare Russian пуска́ть (puskátʹ), imperfective equivalent of пусти́ть (pustítʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pustyni. By surface analysis, пуст (pust, “barren, empty”) + -иня (-inja).

down (soft, fluffy immature feathers which grow on young birds)
to puff, to wheeze, to blow

parole.significato: to become fluffy, to puff up, to fluff up (to become soft, loose, swollen, or fluffy in appearance or texture)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *puxnǫti. By surface analysis, пу́хам (púham) + -на (-na).

parole.significato: to fume, to smoulder, to emit smoke

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bьčeľařь. By surface analysis, пчела (pčela) + -ар (-ar).

parole.significato: to drive away, to chase away, to shoo (force someone or something to leave)
coordinating conjunction used for juxtaposition: however, though
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *pьkъ. Originally a discourse marker, related to Bulgarian по (po, “at, upon”), па (pa, “so, afterwards”).

parole.significato: to crawl, to slither (move at slow speed or on one's knees)

first (preceding all others in a sequence of objects, phenomena, time, or space)

parole.significato: ~ final stage of blooming (the phase in fruit growth when the blossom ripes up and becomes an actual fruit)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьrga (“roast”), whence also Romanian pârgă (“first fruit”).

parole.significato: nimble, brisk, quick, spry, smart, lively, agile, prompt, cracking

parole.significato: to fart, to flatulate (to emit digestive gases from the anus)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pъrtiťь. By surface analysis, пърт (părt, “rag”) (obsolete) + -ищ (-išt).

parole.significato: to open path, to trudge (through hardly traversable terrain)
to flap, to flutter (of wings, fins)
dandruff, scurf (small white or greyish flakes of dead skin from the scalp)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьstry (v-stem). By surface analysis, пъстър (păstăr, “variegated, spotted”) + -ва (-va)

parole.significato: to insert, to infix, to intrude (to place or set something inside somewhere)

sand, sandy (made of, consisting of, or containing sand)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pěsъčьnъ. By surface analysis, пя́сък (pjásăk) + -ен (-en)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orbotьnikъ. By surface analysis, рабо́тя (rabótja, “to work”) + -ник (-nik).

parole.significato: to work (to do a specific task), to labour
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orbotiti, causative-iterative of ра́бота (rábota, “work”) + -я (-ja).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orbotęga. By surface analysis, рабо́тя (rabótja, “to work”) + -яга (-jaga)
From Proto-Slavic *raděti. Cognate with Russian раде́ть (radétʹ, “care for”), Serbo-Croatian радити (“care for”).

parole.significato: for, for the sake of (with the purpose of helping, serving, preserving, or achieving something)

parole.significato: to toil, to be occupied with, to take care of (work, task, obligation)

parole.significato: analysis, examination, discussion (detailed consideration and discussion of the separate aspects, qualities, or feature…
to unroll, to unwrap, to unwind

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orzvodъ, deverbative of разводя́ (razvodjá, “to drive apart”).

From Proto-Slavic *orzlomъ. Morphologically formed as раз- (raz-) + лом (lom, “break, fracture”).

parole.significato: size, dimension, measurement (the physical magnitude, extent, or dimensions of something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orzměrъ. By surface analysis, раз- (raz-) + ме́р (mér)

parole.significato: to ruin, to bankrupt, to impoverish
to unharness, to unyoke, to unhitch an animal from a cart, plough, sledge, etc.
brine, salt water (water with salt dissolved in it, especially used for preserving, pickling, or curing food)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orzsolъ. By surface analysis, раз- (raz-) + сол (sol)

parole.significato: distance (amount of space between two points)
parole.testo: Deverbal noun from разстоя́ (razstojá, “to be at a distance”) + -ние (-nie), from Proto-Slavic *orzstojati.

parole.significato: solution (a homogeneous mixture in which one or more substances are dissolved in another substance)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *orztvorъ. By surface analysis, раз- (raz-) + тво́р (tvór)

Simplified from хрид (hrid) via colloquial elision of initial x-, from Proto-Slavic *xridъ.

parole.significato: brook, creek, beck (small, relatively fast river or stream)

parole.significato: to wake (up), to awaken, to rouse (to make somebody stop sleeping)
to unshoe (footwear, such as shoes, boots, or socks)

From Proto-Slavic *sъ̀nъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *súpnas, from Proto-Indo-European *supnós.

parole.significato: to sip, to slurp; to consume by slurping
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sьrbati, probably of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: heart, cardiac (relating to the heart as an organ)
angry, cross, grumpy, grumpish, ratty, disgruntled, in a huff, huffy

parole.significato: to consume by noisily, to sip; to gurgle (drinks)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sьrkati, probably of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: neighbour (a person living on adjacent or nearby land)

parole.significato: to dry, to dry up, to become dry (to lose moisture or water)

Archaic word for ash gray from Proto-Slavic *śěrъ (“gray”).

parole.significato: mysterious, enigmatic, secretive, inscrutable (difficult to understand, explain, or know; surrounded by mystery)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tajьnьstvenъ. By surface analysis, та́йна (tájna) + -ствен (-stven)

parole.significato: over there, thither, in that direction, over on that side
to respect, to revere, to hold in high esteem
parole.testo: Perhaps inherited from Proto-Slavic *tačiti, originally denoting “to run, flow towards”, a causative-iterative counterpart to essive *tačati (“to roll”) (see there for cognates).

parole.significato: to keep something secret or concealed

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tvorьba. Morphologically equivalent to творя́ (tvorjá, “to create”) + -ба (-ba).

parole.significato: to create, to make, to produce (to bring something into existence, especially by skill, imagination, or effort)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *twírˀtas, from Proto-Indo-European *twerH-.

parole.significato: to claim, to assert, to state, to maintain (to declare something with conviction, usually presenting it as true)

parole.significato: to drag, to pull, to haul

parole.significato: to stomp (with foot or with a bat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tepati, an intensive/iterative variant of Proto-Slavic *tepti.

parole.significato: just from now on, just as of now

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tečьnъ. By surface analysis, тека (teka) + ен (en).

parole.significato: You, thou; the second-person singular pronoun in the nominative case, used as the subject of a verb.

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tiňa, *tina. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic тина (tina), Macedonian тиња (tinja).

parole.significato: to touch, to poke, to prick (with tool)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tipati. Cognate with Slovene típati (“to grope, fumble”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tìskati (“to press, squeeze”). By surface analysis, *tiskъ + -ам (-am).

parole.significato: to run, to sprint, to hare (to move quickly)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tičati, an intensive stem of *tekťi (“to flow, to stream”) (whence Bulgarian тека́ (teká)).
Archaic word for voluntary work, inherited from Proto-Slavic *tolka. Cognate with Lithuanian talkà (“unpaid work”), Latvian tàlka (“party of workers”).

From Proto-Slavic *tratati (a/j-conjugation), related to *tratiti (“to shatter, to waste”).

Deverbal noun of тряскам (trjaskam, “to crack, to pound”) + -а (-a), from Proto-Slavic *trěskъ (“crack, bang”).

From Proto-Slavic *tǫčenъ, a fossilized past passive participle of Proto-Slavic *tǫčiti (“to pour, to flux”).

ear, aural, otic (relating to the ear or ears)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *xabьnъ. By surface analysis, хабя́ (habjá) + -ен (-en).

At least some of the meanings from Proto-Slavic *capati (“to clap, to tramp; to snatch”), of onomatopoeic origin. The rest probably derived by extension.

parole.significato: flower (herbaceous or shrubby plant that serves as decoration)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *květьje (“blossoms”), originally a collective singular only noun. By surface analysis, цвят (cvjat, “blossom”) + -е (-e, collective suffix).

parole.significato: curative, healing, medicinal, salubrious, therapeutic (having the power to heal, cure, or improve health)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *cělьbьnъ. By surface analysis, це́лба (célba) + -ен (-en).
From Proto-Slavic *cělina; equivalent to цял (cjal, “whole, complete”) + -ина (-ina).

parole.significato: to kiss (to touch with the lips)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *cěliti, the causative-iterative of цял (cjal, “whole”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *cěniti, a causative-iterative of Bulgarian цена́ (cená, “price”).

parole.significato: to gradually grow numb, to stiffen, to become motionless
to cleave, to chop, to split by cutting

parole.testo: In spite of the formal difficulties, Anikin considers Proto-Slavic origin and further associates with Lithuanian kỹbras, skiẽbras (“thin, slender”) (with s-mobile). Presumably from Proto-Slavic *cibrъ with rare case of second palatalization before Balto-Slavic *-ei-. Alternatively, from *cěbrъ (< ea

From an earlier Bulgarian чи́рей (čírej), from Proto-Slavic *čirьjь. Equivalent to чир (čir, “ulcer”) (dialectal) + -ей (-ej). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian чи̏р (“ulcer”), Slovene čȋr, čirȃj, Russian чи́рий (čírij), Ukrainian чи́р (čýr), чи́ряк (čýrjak), Polish сzуrеk. Possibly a wanderwort found als

parole.significato: to sulk, to pout, to be in a tiff, to be in a miff

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kvьtěti (ě/i-conjugation). Displaced an earlier *цвьтѫ (*cvʹtǫ), attested in Old Church Slavonic цвисти (cvisti, simple thematic conjugation).

parole.significato: wholeness, entirety, completeness, integrity (the quality or state of being whole, complete, undivided, or intact)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *cělostь. By surface analysis, цял (cjal) + -ост (-ost)
From Proto-Slavic *čajьka, from onomatopoeia of cry ча-ча (ča-ča). Compare Latvian kaija (“mew gull”), Estonian kajakas (“gull”).
From Proto-Slavic *čakati (“to wait, await, expect”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian чекати/čekati, Slovak čakať.

parole.significato: heron, egret (bird of genus Ardea or Egretta)
charm, appeal, attractiveness, enchantment (a strong attractive or captivating quality)
charming, attractive, mesmerizing, captivating (capable of attracting interest)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čarovьnъ. By surface analysis, чар (čar, “charm”) + -о́вен (-óven)

parole.significato: charmer, enchanter (a man who has charm, attractiveness, or personal appeal)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čarovьnikъ. By surface analysis, чар (čar) + -овник (-ovnik).

parole.significato: hour (unit of time: one twenty-fourth of a day, 60 minutes)
to vanish, to disappear (to gradually cease to be seen or heard)
to wait, to await (to remain somewhere or delay action until someone or something comes or happens)
to split, to fork, to span

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čeľadь, formed from a root *čel- (“to grow, to rise as a group”) + -яд (-jad) (collective suffix).

parole.significato: node, snag, knob (of surface or plant)
worm (bilateral protostomic invertebrate with tubular body)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čьrvivъ. Formed as червя (červja, “to redden”) + -ив (-iv). Cognate with Russian черви́вый (červívyj).
From че́рен (čéren, “black”) + дроб (drob, “liver”). This second component ultimately stems from Proto-Slavic *drobъ (literally “organ”).

parole.significato: to draw, to sketch, to scrabble
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čьrtati. By surface analysis, черта́ (čertá, “dash”) + -а́я (-ája).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čьrtežь. By surface analysis, черта́я (čertája, “to draft”) + -еж (-ež).

parole.significato: frequent, common, usual (done or occurring often)

parole.testo: Deverbal from чета́ (četá, “to read”). Diactronically from Proto-Slavic *čьtъ.

parole.significato: bristle (a short, stiff hair, especially on an animal)
read (something that is perceived by reading)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čьtьmo. By surface analysis, чет (čet, “account”) + -мо (-mo).

parole.significato: type of finch (songbird of genus Carduelis)
parole.testo: Of onomatopoeic origin, from the call чи-чи (či-či). Alternatively, from Proto-Slavic *čižь.
From Proto-Slavic *činiti. Cognate with Macedonian чини (čini) and Serbo-Croatian чѝнити / čìniti.
From Proto-Slavic *čitavъ. Morphologically from чит (čit, “integral”) (dialectal, dated) + -ав (-av).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čitаlišče. By surface analysis, чи́там (čítam, “to read, to account”) (dialectal, colloquial) + -алище (-alište).
Baby-talk word, probably reshaped from Proto-Slavic *sьčǫ (“to urinate”) + -кам (-kam).

parole.significato: to languish, to wither, to fade away

parole.testo: Levelled from an earlier чо́фка (čófka), a colloquial variant of Proto-Slavic *čepъka (whence now dialectal Bulgarian чо́пка (čópka)).

parole.significato: via, by means of, with help of
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čerzъ. Doublet of an earlier Old Church Slavonic чрѣсъ (črěsŭ).

parole.significato: to hear (to perceive with the ear)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čuvьstvo, from *čuti (“to sense, feel, notice”) + *-ьstvo.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čudьnъ. Equivalent to чу́до (čúdo) + -ен (-en)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čudovišče. By surface analysis, чу́до (čúdo, “wonder, marvel”) + -овище (-ovište), literally meaning “a marvellous, mystical creature”.

parole.significato: to astonish, to amaze (to make someone feel surprise or wonder)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čuka, limited to South Slavic languages. Compare Lithuanian čiùkaras (“sharp rock”), Latvian čukurs (“ridge”), Serbo-Croatian čuka (“hill; peak”), Albanian çukë (“hill; beak”), Romanian cioc (“beak”), Romanian ciucă (“peak”)), Greek τσούκα (tsoúka, “hill; peak”) or native related
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čukati, at least partially of onomatopoeic origin. Some of the meanings may reflect an e-ablaut of ку́я (kúja, “to hew”) (dialectal) + -кам (-kam).

parole.significato: to perceive, to sense, to get a feeling
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *čutiti (“to perceive, to feel”), possibly merged with the reflex of Proto-Slavic *ťutiti (“to intuit”).

parole.significato: to hear (to perceive with the ear)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čuti (“to feel, to sense”).

parole.significato: small wooden boat, kayak, dugout (carved from a tree log)
to fidget, to budge, to move
seam (the place, line, or junction where two pieces of fabric, leather, or other materials are sewn together)
embroidered row of colorful decorative shapes, commonly seen on Bulgarian traditional attire
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *šьvica (“embroidery”); see also Proto-Slavic *šьvьcь. By surface analysis, шев (šev, “stitch”) + -ица (-ica).

parole.significato: joke, jest (something said or done for amusement)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *šьpъtati, with change of conjugation.

parole.significato: to fuck, to screw, to bang, to shag

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *šivačь. Parsable as ши́вам (šívam, “to sew”) (dialectal) + -ач (-ač).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *šidlo. Equivalent to шия (šija, “to sew”) + -ло (-lo)

parole.significato: thorn, spine, prickle (a sharp pointed outgrowth on a plant)
width, breadth (the measurement of something from side to side)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *širina. By surface analysis, широ́к (širók) + -ина (-ina).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *šija (“collar, link”), derived from the verb (see Etymology 2).

parole.significato: to sew, to stitch, to seam

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *šumьnъ. By surface analysis, шум (šum) + -ен (-en).

parole.significato: to make a noise, to sound, to rustle, to murmur (of rain, leaves, water, etc.)
to gush, to spout (usually accompanied with groaning noise)
parole.testo: Of expressive origin, from Proto-Slavic *šuriti (“to flow rapidly”) + -тя (-tja).

parole.significato: jester, fool (person in a mediaeval royal court)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *šutъ. Cognate to Russian шут (šut).

parole.significato: tanning mush/liqueur used for soaking up leather or another raw material (before processing it)
to spare, to show mercy to (to treat someone with mercy, lenience, or consideration)
stick, staff, baton (usually long and straight)
cub (young of caniformia: dogs, wolves, bears, foxes, musteloidea)
damage, loss, harm (loss or damage, usually material; harm caused to someone or something)
to pinch (to take hold of someone or something between the fingers, teeth, etc. and squeeze)

parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *ščurъ, possibly of onomatopoeic origin.
From щур (štur, “playful, perky”) + -е́ц (-éc), likely stretching back to Proto-Slavic *ščurьcь. Cognate with Macedonian штурец (šturec).
Stative deadjectival from щур (štur, “perky, playful”) + -ея (-eja), possibly extending back to Proto-Slavic *ščurěti.
From Proto-Slavic *ščьrbavъ. Morphologically equivalent to щърба (štărba, “notch, cut, kink”) (dialectal) + -ав (-av).
Etymologically from Proto-Slavic *ǫdolь. By surface analysis, юн- (jun-) + дол (dol, “dale”). Poetic meaning is inherited from Old Church Slavonic ѫдоль (ǫdolĭ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *junakъ, parsable as юн (jun, “juvenile”) (obsolete) + -ак (-ak).
From Proto-Slavic *junь̀cь (“youth”). It is possible for the accent to shift from the second to the first syllable, for reasons unexplained. Cognate with Russian юне́ц (junéc).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫrodъ. By surface analysis, юн- (jun-) + род (rod, “birth, origin”). Poetic meaning is inherited from Old Church Slavonic ѫродъ (ǫrodŭ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *juriti. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian ју́рити.

parole.significato: culinary brine, soup, broth (salty liquid used or left after cooking)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *juxa (“soup”), distantly related to English juice.

parole.significato: apple (the fruit of the tree Malus domestica, chiefly with a green, red, or yellow skin, cultivated in temperate climat…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ablъka. By surface analysis, (obsolete) я́бло (jáblo) + -ка (-ka).
Fossilized locative case of Proto-Slavic *ava (“revelation”), deverbal of causative verb *aviti (“to reveal”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jadъ (“anger”), in case it is distinct from Etymology 2.

parole.significato: furcula, wishbone (forked bone between the neck and breast of a bird)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *(j)ǫdьcь (“small hook, fork”). Cognate with Macedonian јадец (jadec), Serbo-Croatian ја̀дац.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ědivo. By surface analysis, я́да (jáda, “to eat”) + -иво (-ivo)
From Proto-Slavic *ědъšь, past active participle of *ěsti (whence also Bulgarian ям (jam), я́да (jáda, “to eat”)) + -вш (-vš).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ědъkъ (“edible”). By surface analysis, я́да (jáda, “to eat”) + -ък (-ăk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jazvьcь, of unclear further origin.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ājьčьnъ. Morphologically analyzable as яйце́ (jajcé) + -ен (-en).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jarъkъ. Synchronically, equivalent to яра́ (jará, “bright light”) + -ък (-ăk).

parole.significato: to agitate, to spur, to instigate an action or an emotional response
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jariti, parsable as causative-iterative of obsolete Bulgarian яр (jar, “lively, young”).

parole.significato: clear, bright, cloudless (of weather, sky, or light: not dark, gloomy, or cloudy)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *àsenь (n-stem). Doublet of о́сен (ósen).

parole.significato: manger (a trough in a stable or barn for animals to eat from)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *jasli. The singular a-stem is back-formed from original plurale tantum i-stem я́сли pl (jásli).

parole.significato: to become clear, to clear up (to become clearer, more distinct, or easier to perceive)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ěsninа. By surface analysis, я́сен (jásen, “clear, serene”) + -ина (-ina)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ěsnostь. By surface analysis, я́сен (jásen) + -ост (-ost).

parole.significato: clarity, clearness, lucidity (the quality of being clear, understandable, or easy to perceive)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ěsnota. By surface analysis, я́сен (jásen) + -ота (-ota)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *àstrę̄bъ, literally meaning swiftwing. Cognate with Latin accipiter (“hawk”).

parole.significato: liver (the liver; the large internal organ corresponding to modern Bulgarian че́рен дро́б (čéren drób))
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ętro, related to Old Church Slavonic ѧтро (ętro, “liver, entrails”).

parole.significato: to mount on a vehicle/animal for a ride
